514011.title: Henley in Arden
514011.description: Henley-in-Arden is a small market town with a population of about 4000. It is located midway between Solihull and Stratford-upon-Avon and lies on the borders of West Midlands and Warwickshire. It is well served by a good selection of shops, five pubs and ten or so restaurants/wine bars.   The town is a popular spot for the local visitors on a Sunday who arrive in large numbers during the summer months to enjoy a stroll along the High Street and purchase a "Henley Ice cream" from the locally well known Ice Cream Parlour.    Market day is on a Wednesday and from time to time there are livestock markets including the infamous Christmas Turkey Market in December.   The town has a railway station on a local line which runs between Startford-upon Avon and Birmingham and is within 10 minutes of the M40 motorway.

517722.title: Crawley Borough
517722.description: The borough consists of the town of Crawley made up of the town centre plus the following residential neighborhoods:- Bewbush, Broadfield, Furnace Green, Gossops Green, Ifield, Langley Green, Maidenbower, Northgate, Pound Hill, Southgate, Three Bridges, Tilgate, and West Green. In addition the borough includes Gatwick Airport and surrounding area, the Manor Royal industrial estate, and Worth village. It should be noted that the land between Gatwick Airport and the built up area of Crawley contain a number of distinct settlements. The boundaries of the borough are confused by an extension of mainly uninhabited land to the west of Gatwick Airport and a 'pie-slice' cut into the borough below this. As a result of the latter, the outlying parts of Ifield (Ifield Wood) is in Horsham District. From the south, through the east to the north, the M23 and M23/A23 is the boundary, continuing along the northern perimeter of the airport until it's western end, where it heads west to mark the western extension. From the south to the west, the boundary more or less follows the edge of the built up area, curving to the north-east until a kilometre south of the airport when it heads west to mark the western extension. Places in the northern parts of the borough may still retain their Surrey postcodes and addresses, being identified as part of Horley.

517532.title: Pulborough
517532.description: Pulborough is a large village with a population of about 5000. It is located a few miles north of the South Downs and lies at the junction of the River Arun and the river Rother.    Pulborough has glorious views across the river flood plain, a haven for wild life, with the South Downs in the background, and an attractive surrounding countryside.    It has a main line railway station and two small industrial areas.    Pulborough Parish includes the hamlets of Codmore Hill, North Heath and Nutbourne, and is within the Horsham District. It's closest neighbouring villages are Billingshurst, Storrington, Petworth and West Chiltington.

510671.title: Wiltshire
510671.description:
The ceremonial county of Wiltshire consists of two unitary authority areas, governed by Wiltshire Council and Swindon Borough Council.
Wiltshire is the most eastern county of the  South West Region of England,
with  Gloucestershire to the north west,  Somerset to the west and  Dorset to the south west.
In the  South East Region of England, Hampshire is to the south and east,
West Berkshire is to the north of this on the eastern boundary
and on the east boundary of Swindon is Oxfordshire.

510797.title: Aldbourne
510797.description:
Aldbourne is a parish administered by Wiltshire Council, 6 miles north east of  Marlborough,
with its north western boundary with the unitary authority of  Swindon at  Liddington.
The north eastern boundary is with  Baydon.
Aldbourne village is served by the B4192 from Swindon, south east to  Chilton Foliat on the north bank of the River Kennet.
Websites for the area directly south of Aldbourne, are represented by  Ramsbury also on the north bank of the Kennet.
Websites for the area to the south west, in the parish of Mildenhall are included under the Marlborough category,
whereas those for further north in the parishes of Ogbourne St Andrew & Ogbourne St George,
directly west of Albourne Chase, are listed together in the  Ogbourne category.

510816.title: Alderbury
510816.description:
Alderbury is a village in the south of Wiltshire, bypassed by the A36, taking road traffic
from  Salisbury in the north east, to  Southampton in the south east.
The A36 also bypasses the hamlet of Shute End immediately north west of Alderbury village,
and the village of Whaddon, immediately south east.
The parish of Clarendon Park is directly north, represented by  Pitton further north west.
The western parish boundary is the River Avon,  Odstock to the east is only approached
via  Downton directly south.   Whiteparish is directly east.

510703.title: All Cannings
510703.description:
This category lists websites for the Wiltshire parish of All Cannings in the Vale of Pewsey spanning
the Kennet & Avon Canal, 4 miles east of Devizes.
The village of Coate is immediately west, Etchilhampton is to the south west, Patney is to the south,
Beechingstoke is to the south east, and Woodborough is to the east, separated by
the area of  Stanton St Bernard parish south of the canal.
Stanton St Bernard village is north of the canal, on the south slope of All Cannings Down, where Tan Hill is the
second highest hill in Wiltshire (294 metres above sea level, compared with 295 m for Milk Hill north east of Stanton St Bernard).
All Cannings village is on the south bank, which is connected via All Cannings Bridge to the north bank, and the
village of Allington, where websites are included here.  (not the  Allington  near Salisbury ).

510788.title: Allington
510788.description:
There are three areas of Wiltshire known as Allington:
This is not Allington, North Wiltshire,
which is in the parish of Chippenham Without to the north west of the town
south of Kington St Michael parish, where websites are included in the  Chippenham category.
This is not Allington, Kennet, near Devizes:
which is a village in the parish of All Cannings, north of the Kennet & Avon Canal, where websites are included in the  All Cannings category.
This category lists websites for the Wiltshire parish of Allington, north east of Salisbury.
Allington is a village on the A338 north of Boscombe.
Allington parish includes Boscombe but Boscombe Airfield is in  Idmiston parish.
The A338 passes north of the Idmiston village on the way south to  Porton.
Boscombe Down East is east of Allington village within the parish boundary, before  Over Wallop in Hampshire.
Newton Tony village is to the north east of Allington village, east of the A338 on the way to  Cholderton.
before the A303 trunk road, which bypasses  Amesbury to the north west.

1065265.title: Alton
1065265.description:
Alton is the parish containing Alton Barnes with Alton Priors, featuring to the north,
Alton Barnes White Horse, cut into Milk Hill in 1812.
Besides Alton parish, this category lists websites for Stanton St Bernard, the next parish west,
in which Milk Hill rises to 295 metres (968 ft) above sea level, the highest point in Wiltshire.
Wansdyke, a medieval defensive linear earthworks, now part of the White Horse Trial, runs along the ridge
in the north of the parishes from  Huish in the east, and over Tan Hill to  Bishops Cannings in the west.
Stanton St Bernard village is on the north bank of the Kennet and Avon Canal, east of  All Cannings,
and south of Alton Barnes, the hamlet of Honeystreet straddles the canal, before it curves
south of Woodborough Hill, eastwards down  Vale of Pewsey.

510809.description:
Ansty is a village in south west Wiltshire, immediately west of  Swallowcliffe, north
of the A30 taking road traffic east towards  Shaftesbury.
Ansty parish stretches south of the A30 to Alvediston before  Berwick St John further south west.
Donhead St Andrew is directly west, and the south west extremes
of  Tisbury parish are directly north.

links.title: Ansty PYO and Farm Shop
links.description: Profile and product range. Includes information about its maize maze.

links.title: Rob Beale Limited
links.description: A company offering liquid waste disposal, septic tank emptying, temporary toilet hire, security fencing and container hire. Company profile, products and contacts.

510821.title: Arts and Entertainment
510821.description: This category includes sites about local artistic, cultural and entertainment activities, events, institutions, businesses and organisations.

links.title: Wylye Valley Art Trail 2003
links.description: Describes a celebration of arts which took place over 9 days in May 2003. Includes profiles of participating artists.

links.title: The Sound Post
links.description: Suppliers of violins, cellos, basses, violas, strings, and accessories to the UK retail trade.

links.title: Wiltshire Folk Arts
links.description: An organisation that researches, collects and re-enacts traditional music, song, customs and traditions of Wiltshire. Includes  a newsletter.

links.title: Rural Arts Wiltshire
links.description: Organisation bringing arts events to rural communities throughout the county.  Events, bookings, mailing list and other contact information.

links.title: Mark Hankinson
links.description: A sporting and animal artist. Profile and portfolio. Bowerchalke.

links.title: Francis Farmar
links.description: A painter in oils and watercolour. Biography, gallery and contacts. Sedgehill.

links.title: Vintage Nostalgia Festival
links.description: Annual Spring event with glamping facilities, entertainment, classic vehicles for sale. Includes prices and location at Stockton Park.

links.title: Wiltshire Historic Churches Trust
links.description: Independent, non-profit organisation promoting and supporting church buildings of historic, architectural and community value across the county. Overview of buildings, publications, grants, support and contacts.

links.title: Georgina Crisford
links.description: Painter and artist, with portfolio, exhibitions and blog.

links.title: Akabella
links.description: Single page profile of this acapella group. Future events and booking details.

510772.title: Ashton Keynes
510772.description:
Ashton Keynes is a village and north Wiltshire parish, which includes the Cotswold Water Park, south of the
Gloucestershire parishes of Ewen, Siddlington and  South Cerney south of  Cirencester.
Oaksey is to the west, where websites are included to the A429 opposite Cotswold Airport.
Upper Minety next south is within the parish of  Minety, which represents Leigh parish, whereas Chelworth
Lower Green and Chelworth Upper Green are within the parish of  Cricklade to the east.

links.title: Ashton Keynes Online
links.description: Community information including local business and forthcoming events.

links.title: Ashton Keynes Village Hall
links.description: Facilities, what's on, availability, and prices.

510880.title: Atworth
510880.description:
Atworth is a village on the A365 between  Box and  Melksham.
The northern boundary of the parish Atworth follows the remains of a Roman road from
Silchester to Bath, with  Corsham parish to the north.
Atworth parish extends south of the village to include the hamlet of Little Chalfield and the
village of Great Chalfield, north of  Holt, where  Broughton Gifford is to the east.

links.title: Stonar School
links.description: Information and admission details for independent school taking boarding girls 8 to 18, day girls 2 to 18 and day boys 2 to 8.

links.title: KA Spencer
links.description: Provider of software and computer services. Includes information on products, services, and contacts.

links.title: Atworth Village
links.description: Gives an overview of information on organisations and activities within and around the village.

links.title: Church Farm
links.description: Photographs and details of bed and breakfast accommodation on a working dairy farm, contacts for location.

510706.title: Avebury
510706.description:
Avebury is parish administered by Wiltshire Council, 6 miles west of Marlborough.
Within the parish the postal addresses refer to the towns of Calne and Chippenham.
The village of Avebury is north of the A4 main road from Marlborough to Calne,
and traffic passes through the village from Devizes in the south taking the A4361 to Swindon.
Although now a rural village, it was once the centre of a primitive race, and its archaeological remains
attract visitors, especially the UNESCO World Heritage site for “Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites”

links.title: Avebury Henge Shop
links.description: Sells guides and books on archaeology and history plus jewellery, pottery, clothes and gifts.  Includes information on the shop and Avebury.

links.title: Avebury Vocal Ensemble
links.description: A chamber choir conducted by Sir Peter Beale. Profile, concerts and contacts.

links.title: Avebury Cricket Club
links.description: Information on fixtures, results, players, averages, grounds, and events. Members of the Wiltshire Cricket League.

links.title: A Present From the Past
links.description: A detailed description of the ancient monuments in the area including full information regarding the most recent discoveries.

links.title: Avebury Stones
links.description: Pictures and details of the stone circle and henge monument.

links.title: Stonehenge.co.uk
links.description: Guide and history of megaliths and their myths, Summer Solstice Celebrations, with photographs and information for visitors.

510754.title: Barford St Martin
510754.description:
Barford St Martin is a village north of the A30 west of  Wilton and east of  Fovant.
North of the River Nadder, the B3089 leads west to  Dinton.
North of the village Barford Down rises to Grovely Wood which conceals the remains of Grim's Ditch and a Roman road.

links.title: Barford St Martin Parish Council
links.description: Details about the local tier of government, also contains information on history of village, church, amenities and local history group, with social media link.

links.title: The Barford Inn
links.description: A sixteenth century former coaching inn offering en-suite bedrooms in a first floor annexe. Includes information on facilities, events, location and links to community resources.

1063583.title: Baydon
1063583.description:
Baydon is the most north eastern parish administered by Wiltshire Council, before the unitary authority boundary
with  Swindon at Wanborough parish, where the M4 motorway passes to the north east of Baydon village.
The eastern parish boundary councides with the unitary authority boundary with West Berkshire at  Lambourn.
The rural area to the south east features the Iron Age hill fort of Membury, giving its name to the M4 services.
which is north of the Wiltshire parish of  Chilton Foliat on the north bank of the River Kennet.
Websites for the area directly south of Baydon, are represented by  Ramsbury, also on the north bank of the Kennet.
The Wiltshire parish of  Albourne is directly west of Baydon.

links.title: Baydon St Nicholas
links.description: Church of England VA primary school presents governers, staff and council, with overview of classes, information for parents, friends and community, including contacts and location.

links.title: Baydon Village
links.description: Guide including Wiltshire and parish council meetings, overview of amenities including post office, the Red Lion, St Nicholas church and school, local clubs and related links.

1064914.title: Berwick St John
1064914.description:
Berwick St John is a village and parish on the northern edge of Cranborne Chase in the west of Wiltshire,
The village is south of the A30 road, linking  Shaftesbury from the north west to  Swallowcliffe.
Donhead St Mary is to the west, and  Bower Chalke is directly east.

links.title: Berwick St James
links.description: Community pages with local history, pictures, notices and events, Berwick Fete and Dog Show and a list of local businesses.

links.title: The Forge
links.description: Offers blacksmithing, fabrication and wrought iron repairs. Overview of services, project gallery, opening times, contacts and location.

links.title: Gable Cottage
links.description: Offers three bedrooms for self catering holidays. Profile, places to visit, things to do, details of rooms and facilities, tariff, contacts and booking link.

510700.title: Biddestone
510700.description:
This category represents the parish of Biddestone, which has a village directly west of  Chippenham,
south of the A420 road and north of the A4 at  Corsham.
The smaller village of Slaughterford is directly west, on the east bank of By Brook, which forms the
western boundary of Biddestone parish.
On the A420 north west, the village of Ford in the parish of  North Wraxall.

links.title: Delphiniums
links.description: Information about delphinium species grown in David and Shirley Bassett's garden.

links.title: Anvil Cottage
links.description: Holiday cottage sleeping four and set in the grounds of an 18th century manor house. Profile, facilities and tariff.

510701.title: Recreation and Sports
510701.description: This category includes all hobbies, sports and participatory recreational activities, including local organisations.

links.title: Biddestone Tennis Club
links.description: Match fixture lists, Wiltshire league results, Biddestone tennis club membership details and committee minutes.

links.title: Biddestone Cricket Club
links.description: Fixtures and results, league details, information for members, averages and archives.

510702.title: Football
510702.description: This category includes all hobbies, sports and participatory recreational activities, including local organisations.

1064997.title: Bishops Cannings
1064997.description:
Bishops Cannings is a village east of the A361, north east of  Devizes, from  Avebury in the north east.
Bishops Cannings parish is in the Vale of Pewsey, with Roundway Hill to the north west,
featuring the Devizes Millennium White Horse, cut in 1999.
At the south of the parish, the Kennet and Avon Canal wind round the base of hills from  All Cannings in
the east, almost encirling the hamlet of Horton before entering Roundway parish north of Devizes.
Little Horton and Coate are within the parish to the south before Etchilhampton.

links.title: North Wilts Golf Club
links.description: An 18 hole downland golf course offering views of the Wiltshire countryside.

links.title: The Crown Inn
links.description: Restaurant with a pub campsite offering pitches for tents & motorhomes. Describes their facilities, events, menus, menus, opening hours, availability, booking contacts and links to social media.

links.title: Bishops Cannings Youth Action Group
links.description: Formed in 2007 aiming to provide facilities for the parish's young, and organising activities. Includes history, their field and events, with committee details.

510859.title: Bishopstone
510859.description:
There is also a Bishopston­e parish in Swindon's unitary authority, on the boundary with Oxfordshire,
where websites for Bishopston­e village are included in the  Hinton Parva category.
Bishopston­e is a village on the north bank of the River Ebble in south Wiltshire, and Bishopston­e parish includes the
hamlets of Croucheston on the south bank, and The Pitts on higher ground to the east,
towards Stratford Toney downstream, before  Coombe Bissett further east.
Broad Chalke parish is upstream to the west, and the parish extends over
Cranborne Chase to the Hampshire border to the south.

links.title: Helen Browning’s Organic
links.description: Philosophies of this organic farm, and details of how to purchase its organic products.

1064967.title: Blunsdon
1064967.description:
Blunsdon is a civil parish in the Borough of Swindon, and this category includes St Andrew separated by the A419
taking road traffic north west to  Cricklade.The southern boundary of Blunsdon St Andrew is the A4198 ring road.
Broad Blunsdon village is to the east of the A419, and Stanton Fitzwarren parish is further east.
The Swindon borough parishes of Hannington is to the north east, represented by the  Highworth category.

1064712.title: Bowerchalke
1064712.description:
Bowerchalk­e is a village, on the north edge of Cranborne Chase in the west of Wiltshire.
Minor roads in the south of Bower Chalke parish lead over the Chase to the Dorset parishes
of  Pentridge and  Sixpenny Handley, where the A354 leads to Hampshire at Martin
represented by the  Damerham category.
Broad Chalke is to the north east and the next parish west is  Berwick St John.

links.title: Chalke Valley History Festival
links.description: Information for visitors, schools, traders, business sponsors, opportunities, volunteering, membership, videos and social media links.

510771.title: Box
510771.description:
This category represents the parish of Box, which besides the large village of this name, stretches east
to include Box Hill, rising on the east bank of By Brook, and Rudloe, west of  Corsham.
The parish western boundary coincides with the unitary authority boundary with  Bath & NES at  Batheaston,
on the A4 road through Box from the north of Corsham.
Box parish includes Kingsdown south of By Brook, with Middlehill and Ditteridge to the north before  Colerne.
From the A4 at Box, the A365 road leads south east through  Atworth
on the way to  Melksham further south east.
The parish south of Kingsdown is  Monkton Farleigh, which also represents
South Wraxall, the parish to the south east, before Atworth.

links.title: Malcolm Smith Power Washing
links.description: High pressure washing, sanitising and graffiti removal within 100 miles of Box.

links.title: Bybrook House Nursing Home
links.description: Provides residential care for the elderly in a rural setting. Photographs and activities available.

links.title: Real World Studios
links.description: Information about facilities and staff at Peter Gabriel's  recording studios.

links.title: Lorne House Bed and Breakfast
links.description: A family run guesthouse. Includes room details, prices, local attractions and booking form.

links.title: Jacqui Jarosy
links.description: Therapist offering relaxation, yoga and complementary therapy including massage, reflexology and counselling.

links.title: J Price Bath
links.description: Manufacturers of tennis balls and an assortment of rubber products. Company information and contact details.

links.title: Hann Made Carpentry & Joinery Ltd.
links.description: Offers doors, windows and staircases together with free-standing and built-in furniture. Profile, roduct range, services and contacts.

links.title: Lower Rudloe Farm
links.description: Offers self-catering and bed and breakfast accommodation, with yoga retreat, wedding venue, farm shop and cinema evenings. Details of facilities, photo gallery, information on local events, attractions, contacts and location west of the town.

links.title: Logs Near Me
links.description: Family owned specialist supplier of kiln dried firewood and briquettes. Profile, catalogue, prices, delivery terms, blog, and social media link.

links.title: Rudloe Scene
links.description: Articles and photos of an area that straddles the Cotswold AONB east of Box Hill, with history, characters, events, news and contact form.

510755.title: Bradford-on-Avon
510755.description:
This category lists websites for the town and Wiltshire parish of Bradford-on-Avon,
which has one of the oldest multiple arch bridges.
The bridge carries road traffic south on the A363 to  Trowbridge, having wound through the town centre from  Bathford.
The B3107 road leads east to  Holt, and before this, intersection by
the B3105 leads across the Avon to  Staverton.
On the north bank, the B3108 road leads west through  Winsley before a bridge over
the Avon, then under the railway at  Limpley Stoke.
South of the Avon, the parish of  Westwood directly west, represents Avoncliff.

links.title: Aukana Trust
links.description: Meditation centre which was established for those in search of a practical approach to the Buddha's path to enlightenment. Includes FAQ, diary dates and contact.

links.title: Bradford-on-Avon Lifesaving and Lifeguard Club
links.description: Information about the club's activities, news and a calendar of events.

links.title: Bradford on Avon History
links.description: A collection of maps, photographs and other sources for local history and genealogy. Includes histories for a number of houses, family trees and 18th-century voters lists.

links.title: Bradford on Avon Amateur Swimming Club
links.description: Caters for learners, competitive swimmers and water polo.  Detailed information on the organisation, programmes and personnel of the club, plus news and a calendar.

links.title: Bradford on Avon Town Council
links.description: Includes details of councillors, meetings, policies and projects.

links.title: Workplace Wellness
links.description: The team of GPs and OH specialist nurses provide Occupational Health Services to organisations of all sizes. The service covers health surveillance, noise conservation, case management and work station assessment.

links.title: Kingston Archery Club
links.description: Information, history, photographs, beginners courses, social, events, and links.

links.title: St Laurence School
links.description: Information on governance, links for students, staff, carers and parents, its news, dates, facilities hire, contacts and location.

links.title: Wiltshire Music Centre
links.description: A 300 seat concert hall plus nine teaching and workshop spaces of various sizes. Profile, what's on, contacts and social media links.

links.title: The Bradfordians Dramatic Society
links.description: Information about meetings and joining up. Also lists past and current productions.

links.title: Bradford on Avon Film Society
links.description: Newsletter, full programme and archive.

510760.title: Business and Economy
510760.description: This category includes sites covering the business and economic activities of the town, including listings of most companies and industries.

links.title: Ashford Homes (South Western) Ltd.
links.description: Constructor of individually designed housing.

links.title: Maplecroft Consultants
links.description: Professional facilitation programmes to optimise stakeholder dialogue and manage change effectively. Includes overview of services and staff profiles.

links.title: Westdale Nurseries
links.description: Particular emphasis on Bougainvilleas and Hydrostore. Offers tips on how to make hanging baskets.

links.title: The Lock Inn
links.description: Local cafe. Also has a bike shop, and bike and boat hire.

links.title: Enfusion
links.description: Environmental planning consultants.

links.title: Perfect Day
links.description: Bridal wear, accessories and evening wear. Details of collections and sizes in stock, location and opening times.

links.title: Wildlife Art Prints by Ann Seward
links.description: Specialising in commissioned pet portraits and limited edition prints of wildlife art portraits in watercolour and in fine pencil prints, with online sales.

links.title: Young Blooms
links.description: Florists specialising in wedding flowers and hand-crafted bouquets. Photographs and prices.

links.title: Overt Design
links.description: Website designer covering South West region. Portfolio with reference customer designs.

links.title: Brighterside
links.description: Explains the company philosophy of simple and concise web design. Biography, portfolio and blog.

links.title: Sally Boats Ltd
links.description: Offering a fleet of narrowboats for hire on the Kennet and Avon Canal. Includes charges and availability.

links.title: T and A Motors
links.description: Service, MOT and repair centre. Advice on car maintenance and air conditioning, with contacts at the south edge of town.

510759.title: Health
510759.description: Includes health and medical resources specific to

links.title: Denise Darroch
links.description: Psychotherapist offering therapy, counselling and psychotherapy.

links.title: Homeopathy UK
links.description: Profile, therapies and conditions treated.

510756.title: Travel and Tourism
510756.description: This category includes sites for area attractions and resources for those travelling to the town, including tourist guides.

links.title: Bradford on Avon Tourist Office
links.description: Information about transport, accommodation and things to see.

links.title: Willow Barn
links.description: A restored barn to let for self-catering holidays in the village of Holt. Details of accommodation, facilities and local attractions.

links.title: Stag Web
links.description: Organisers of stag weekends in Ireland, the UK and Europe. Details of packages available, activities, contact information and enquiry form.

links.title: Bradford-on-Avon Tithe Barn
links.description: Opening times for the medieval tithe barn.

links.title: Visit Bradford On Avon
links.description: Directory for tourists to find out whats on, where to stay and what to do in the town and the surrounding area.

510757.title: Accommodation
510757.description: This category includes directories, reservation services and individual sites for temporary accommodation, primarily for travellers.

links.title: Beeches Farmhouse and Pig Wig Cottages
links.description: Provides details of an 18th century house, with ensuite rooms and self catering cottages, with tariff and contacts for location east of the town.

links.title: Widbrook Grange Hotel
links.description: Country house situated in acres of grounds. Facilities, tariff, and contacts for location south of the town.

links.title: Lynchetts
links.description: Description, photos and prices for this bed and breakfast.

links.title: Leigh House
links.description: Sixteenth century stone farmhouse, converted barn and bakehouse, with gym and sauna for guests. History, details of facilities, including weddings, prices, and contacts for location north of the town.

links.title: Woolley Grange Hotel
links.description: Hotel and spa, with glamping suites. Overview of accommodation, facilities, details of special breaks, online booking and contacts, with social media links.

1065177.title: Bratton
1065177.description:
Bratton is a village on the B3098 road north of Salisbury Plain, east of  Westbury,
and west of  Edington.
Minor roads lead to  Steeple Ashton parish immediately north.

1064959.title: Bremhill
1064959.description:
Bremhill is a village in west Wiltshire, immediately north west of  Calne.
The River Marden flows through the south of Bremhill parish on its way to the River Avon which forms
the western parish boundary with Langley Burrell Without parish, north west of  Chippenham.
The villages of East Tytherton and Tytherton Lucas, are west of Bremhill village before Langley Burrell.
Charlcutt and Spirthill are hamlets north of Bremhill village, and
Foxham village is further north before  Christian Malford.
Catcomb is a hamlet on the north east boundary, before  Lyneham and Bradstoke parish.
Cowage Brook forms the eastern boundary with  Hilmarton.

links.title: Bremhill Village
links.description: Community resource presenting parish councillor contacts, amenities, weather, village hall events, local businesses, newsletter archive, news blog and related links.

links.title: Bremhill Parish Council
links.description: Local tier of government for four villages; Bremhill, Foxham, East Tytherton and Tytherton Lucas, and the hamlets of Charlcutt, Spirthill, Stanley Lane, Stanley, Avon, and Bremhill Wick. Includes meeting records, plans, consultation, organisations, calendar, newsletter and downloads.

links.title: GB Motorcycles
links.description: Specialist in British brands, offers bikes for sale, service and delivery terms, news blog, opening times and contacts for viewing at Charlcutt.

510768.title: Brinkworth
510768.description:
Brinkworth is a village and parish west of  Royal Wootton Bassett.
The B4042 takes road traffic westwards to Little Somerford.
The parish includes the hamlets of Braydon Side, Callow Hill, The Common,
and includes Grittenham now south of the M4 motorway.

links.title: Jamie Railton Bloodstock Agent
links.description: Services and facilities from specialists in the preparation of thoroughbred horses for public auction.

links.title: Virtual Business Centre Ltd
links.description: Offers telephone answering, telemarketing, secretarial support, IT consultancy and support.

links.title: Brinkworth on the Web
links.description: Community site including news, webcam and updated weather.

links.title: Brinkworth House Business & Events Centre
links.description: Offers serviced office accommodation.

links.title: Watson Fuels
links.description: Nationwide distribution of oil and petroleum products for domestic and commercial use. Details of site locations and on-line ordering.

510769.title: Broad Chalke
510769.description:
Broad Chalke, sometimes spelled Broadchalke, Broad Chalk or Broadchalk, is a village and civil parish in
south Wiltshire, and includes the hamlets of Knapp, Mount Sorrel and Stoke Farthing.
Bower Chalke parish separates Broad Chalke from the border with north East Dorset at  Pentridge.

links.title: Gurston Down Hillclimb
links.description: Automobile Racing Club. Hosts an annual championship and challenge, and is visited twice a year by the National Championship contenders. Provides specialist tuition.

links.title: Broad Chalke Primary School
links.description: Resource for parents and pupils of the school, providing news, staff, calendar and curriculum information.

links.title: Chalke Valley Sports Centre
links.description: Information on facilities, related clubs and their matches.

510844.title: Broad Hinton
510844.description:
This category lists websites for the Wiltshire Council parish of Broad Hinton with its village on the A4361, 5 miles south west of  Swindon.
Broad Hinton parish includes the hamlet of Uffcott on the boundary of Swindon borough before  Wroughton to the north east.
Broad Town village and parish is to the north west.
Clyffe Pypard village and parish is next to the west, and  Winterbourne Bassett is next south on the A4361.
A minor road leads up Hackpen Hill to the east, south of Barbury Castle, to  Ogbourne Maizey, which is east of the
Marlborough Downs.  There is a White Horse figure at the south east tip of Broad Hinton parish, before Preshute Down.
Preshute parish, is over the Marlborough Downs, represented by the  Marlborough category.

links.title: The Crown Inn
links.description: A public house offering food, AccommodationFacility detailsdrink and accommodation. Profile, facility details, food, bar, and contacts.

links.title: Broad Hinton
links.description: A community web site for the village and surrounding area. The village, clubs, business, the council, and general information.

links.title: Broad Town C of E Primary School
links.description: News and information for parents, pupils and the general public. Including newsletters and school prospectus.

links.title: Broad Hinton Primary School
links.description: The school, news, classes, photographs, and contacts.

1064975.title: Brokenborough
1064975.description:
Brokenborough parish is north west of  Malmesbury, just south west of Hankerton parish, where the B4014 road
leads to Long Newton in the  Cotswold district of Gloucestershire.
Crudwell is north on the A429, after taking road traffic through the western edge of Malmesbury.
Besides Brokenboro­ugh and western parts of Hankerton parish, this category lists websites for Easton Grey
along the county boundary before  Sherston, where the Sherston branch of the River Avon
forms the southern boundary of the parishes.

links.title: Whatley Manor
links.description: Provides details and photographs of the accommodation, restaurant, spa, and conference facilities. Link for online booking and contacts.

1064966.title: Bromham
1064966.description:
Bromham is a village, which with the hamlet of Westbrook is on the A3102 road east of  Melksham,
before it joins the A342, south of  Chippenham and north of  Devizes.
Bromham parish is directly north west of  Rowde.
Roundway parish is represented by the Devizes category, before Heddington north of Beacon Hill,
where websites may be listed here, but those for further north including Derry Hill
should be listed in the  Calne category.
Bowden Hill to the north west is within the  Lacock parish,
before the River Avon at Beanacre north of Melksham.

links.title: Wayside
links.description: Offer rural bed and breakfast accommodation, or or self catering lodges, featuring guest use of Chittoe Heath Plantation woodland. Facilities range, tourist information, tariffs, contacts and directions for location.

links.title: Bromham Village
links.description: Local guide including information about the parish council, clerk contacts, plans, notice board, the Bromham Hoot newsletter archive, photo gallery and related links.

510693.title: Broughton Gifford
510693.description:
This category lists websites for the Wiltshire Council parish of Broughton Gifford directly west
of  Melksham, south of  Atworth and east of its parish at Great Chalfield.
Broughton Gifford parish southern boundary is the River Avon, which continues as
the southern boundary of  Holt on the B3107 road, to the south west.

links.title: Wiltshire Trail Riders Fellowship
links.description: Forthcoming events, news and information as well as directions to meeting venue.

510814.title: Burbage
510814.description:
Burbage is a village bypaassed to the west by the A346, taking road traffic south from  Marlborough to join the A338
south of the village, which continues south through  Tidworth to join the A303 at  Cholerton.
The A338 comes from the east through East Grafton in the neighbouring  Grafton parish.
At this roundabout, the B3087 leads west to  Pewsey, passing first through Easton,
before Milton Lilbourne.
Websites for Milton Lilbourne are included with Pewsey, whereas those for Easton are listed here.
The north of Burbage parish includes the Kennet and Avon Canal.
North east of the hamlet of Stibb Green, the canal passes under Bruce Tunnel, where a minor road connects the hamlet
of Durley, which takes road traffic through the hamlet of The Warren, before the parish boundary with  Little Bedwyn.
Great Bedwyn is the neighbouring parish on the canal's north bank, west of Crofton Locks.
on the north west tip of Grafton parish.
Savernake is to the north west of the canal, which also represents Wooton Rivers on the canal to the west of the
Burbage hamlet of Ram Alley, and Westcourt is west of the A346.
The parish also includes the hamlets of Eastcourt and Marr Green.

links.title: Wikipedia: Burbage
links.description: Article describing the village, its history, amenities, geography of the area, with references and related links.

links.title: Plum-IT Services
links.description: Offers plumbing and central heating engineering services. Profile, capabilities, area covered and portfolio with testimonials.

links.title: Gary Witheford
links.description: Equine behaviourist outlines his methods, case studies, and forthcoming shows and clinics.

links.title: Westcourt Bottom
links.description: Accommodation in 17th century cottage, also artists studios. Includes photos and list of rooms, facilities and rates.

links.title: White Horse Boats
links.description: Offers narrowboats for holiday hire on the Kennet and Avon Canal, and seasonal public trips by arrangement. Details of craft, FAQ, guide, routes including information on Wiltshire's white horses, videos, photo gallery, blog, booking availability and contacts.

510707.title: Burcombe
510707.description:
Burcombe is a village south of the A30 west of  Wilton and east of  Barford St Martin.
The main village is south of the River Nadder, but a bridge links to the A30 at North Burcombe, and
the church is north of this and south of the railway line.
The parish of Burcombe Without continues up the hill to the north to Great Wishford parish, and
south of the village the parish rises up the hill to  Bishopstone parish.
The hamlet of Bulbridge downstream, south of the Nadder provides the nearest primary school, but is in Wilton parish.

510774.title: Calne
510774.description:
Calne is a town in north west Wiltshire, east of  Chippenham
on the A4 road from  Avebury in the east.
Calne Without is the parish to the south west on the A3102, which joins the A342 before Bromham to the south.
North of the A4 east of the town, the River Marden flows through the south of  Bremhill parish on its way to the River Avon.
North of the town, the A3102 takes road traffic through  Hilmarton on the way to  Lyneham.
This category also includes websites for Cherhill on the A4 to the east.

510805.title: Castle Combe
510805.description:
Castle Combe is a village nestled in a valley through which Broadmead Brook flows in the Cotswolds AONB in north west Wiltshire.
Castle Combe parish includes Upper Castle Combe uphill to the west.
The plateau to the south east of the parish is home for motorsports, before  Yatton Keynell on the B4039 road.
Broadmead Brook flows to the south of the parish at the village of Ford on the A420, which leads to 
North Wraxall eastwards, both within the parish of North Wraxall on Castle Combe's western boundary.
Castle Coombe parish is separated from the South Gloucestershire boundary by  Nettleton to the north west.

links.description: Fourteenth century country house hotel. Includes details of bedrooms, restaurants, golf course, grounds and local area.

1064976.title: Castle Eaton
1064976.description:
Castle Eaton is a civil parish in the Swindon unitary authority, north west of  Highworth on the boundary
of Wiltshire Council at Latton and  Marston Maisey.
The northern parish boundary is the Isis part of the  River Thames, with the 
Cotswold district of Gloucestershire at Kempsford south of  Fairford, and forming the
northern boundary of Swindon unitary authority into Oxfordshire.
The hamlet of Hannington Wick is to the south east, in the parish of Hannington before Highworth,
and this category includes websites for north of Swanborough.

510712.title: Chapmanslade
510712.description:
Chapmanslade is a village and Wiltshire parish on the border with Somerset Mendips at  Frome.
Chapmanslade parish includes the hamlets of Huntenhull Green, Short Street and Thoulstone.
The village is served by the A3098 from  Westbury to the north east.
Warminster is to the south east via the A36.
Corsley Heath is directly south in the parish of  Corsley.

510728.title: Charlton
510728.description:
(Note:  Not to be confused with the parish between Rushall and Wilsford, where websites should be listed with the parish of  Upavon.)
This category lists websites from the area north and east of  Malmesbury.
Charlton is the parish immediately north of Milbourne, a hamlet in Malmesbury parish, and Garsden in the
combined parish of Lea and Cleverton. north of  Little Somerford. 
Brokenborough parish is north west of Malmesbury, where the B4014 road leads to Long Newton in
the  Cotswold district of Gloucestershire.
Crudwell is north of Charlton on the A429, after taking road traffic through the western edge of Hankerton parish,
where Hankerton village is directly north of Charlton village.
Minety is to the north east of Hankerton parish.

510688.title: Chilmark
510688.description:
Chilmark is a village in south west Wiltshire on the B3089 road from  Teffont over the Ridge to  Fonthill Bishop.
Chilmark parish includes the hamlets of Mooray and Portash, towards Lower and Upper
Chickgrove on the north bank of the River Nadder.
Tisbury is to the south west, and  Sutton Mandeville is south of the River Nadder to the south east.

links.title: Winterbourne Cottage
links.description: Self catering accommodation, with information on facilities, prices and availability.

1065122.title: Chilton Foliat
1065122.description:
Chilton Foliat is a village on the B4192 road from  Ramsbury directly west, through which the River Kennet
flows south of the village across the West Berkshire boundary into  Hungerford to the south east.
The B4001 road heads north of the village towards  Lambourn.
The hamlet of Crooked Soley is in the north of Chilton Foliat parish, before Whittonditch
in Ramsbury parish, south of  Aldbourne.

510881.title: Chippenham
510881.description:
This category lists websites for the town and Wiltshire parish of Chippenham, which is bypassed to the west by the A350,
between  Melksham, and north to Junction 17 of the M4 motorway, before the A429 to  Melksham further north.
Besides the town, this category lists websites in the hamlets such as Allington north west of the bypass,
in the parish of Chippenham Without, but those further north are included with  Kingsley Langley.
Biddestone is to the west, and  Corsham is to the south west. 
Lacock is to the south, and Derry Hill to the south east is represented by  Calne further east.
East of the River Marden, websites are listed in   Bremhill parish, and the confluence of the River Marden with the
River Avon is north east of the town, in the parish of Langley Burrell which is represented by the Kingsley Langley category.

510857.title: Chiseldon
510857.description:
Chiseldon is a civil parish in the Swindon unitary authority, south east of Central Swindon
The M4 motorway coincides with the northern parish boundary, and the eastern boundary
with Liddington is east of the A346 road.
In the south east of the parish the A346 becomes the unitary authority boundary, with the
Wiltshire Council parish of  Ogbourne at Ogbourne St George.
The main conurbation is west of the A346, and the parish extends west, to  Wroughton,
which is south west of Central Swindon.

links.description: Details of the junior and senior teams, club news, player statistics, and fixtures and results.

1065208.title: Chitterne
1065208.description:
Chitterne is a village on the southern edge of Salisbury Plain, on the B390 road west of  Shrewton.
To the west, the B390 meets the A36 to  Warminster at Heytesbury.
Before this, the B390 passes through the small parish of Knock, whose boundary extends north
along the western boundary of Chitterne parish.
Upton Lovell is immediately west of Chitterne parish.
Codford parish is along the southern boundary, which represents the Wylye valley east of the A303 road.
South east of Chitterne Down, the remains of Yarnborough Castle hill fort are north of the A303 on
the boundary between  Steeple Langford and  Berwick St James before Maddington Down
in Shrewton on the eastern boundary.
Orcheston is north of Shrewton, and a minor road connects Chitterne north east to  Tilshead.
The northern boundary is between Berril Down and Chapperton Down in Imber, where the
army training area is represented by the Tilshead category.

links.title: Chitterne
links.description: An introduction to this village and the south of Salisbury Plain. Includes history, location map, photographs and information on village life, parish council and the village hall, with link to social media.

links.title: Chitterne Now and Then
links.description: Blog maintained by Sue Robinson featuring contemporary and old photographs, to illustrate buildings, landmark changes and walks around the area.

links.title: Sue Robinson
links.description: Local historian presents biography, featuring voluntary group of women stitching kneelers for All Saints’ and St Mary’s Church, history of the Round House, and links to her contributions to the village's online presence.

510767.title: Cholderton
510767.description:
Cholderton is a village on the A338, and a Wiltshire parish on the boundary with Hampshire, just south of
the A303 trunk road between  Amesbury in the west and  Andover to the east.
To the north of the A303, the 338 leads to  Shipton Bellinger.
To the east, south of A303, are the Hampshire parishes of  Thruxton and Quarley,
between which is the western extreme of Monxton parish.
Despite Cholderton Park being in this part of Monxton, websites for this area are included here.
Wilbury park is south of the parish boundary with Newton Tony for which websites area also listed here.
Allington is the next parish south on the A338, which lists websites for Boscombe Down,
which are south and east of Amesbury parish.

links.title: Cholderton Rare Breeds Farm
links.description: Activity park with rare breed animals, also offering a wedding venue. Information on their facilities, shop and hostel accommodation.

links.title: Michael's Wood
links.description: Woodland burials site. Profile, facilities and ethos.

1059537.title: Christian Malford
1059537.description:
Christian Malford is a village in west Wiltshire, on the eastern bank of the River Avon which forms
the western parish boundary with  Sutton Benger, and the northern boundary with  Seagry
and  Great Somerford at the parish's northern tip before  Dauntsey to the north east.
Bradenstoke and Lyneham Airfield are across the east boundary represented by the  Lyneham category.
Foxham village is immediately south in the parish of  Bremhill.

links.title: Tigerplay Ltd.
links.description: Indoor and soft play equipment specialists offering children's play centres.

1065162.title: Chute
1065162.description:
Chute is a Wiltshire Council parish on the border with Hampshire at  Tangley.
The main conurbation is Upper Chute, but with smaller settlements collectively known as The Chutes.
Chute Forest has its own parish south east of Lower Chute, Chute Standen and Chute Cadley.
Conholt Park is on the north east boundary of Chute parish, where the northern boundary follows
the course of Grim's Ditch, with the Roman road, Chute causeway, within the parish until
it heads north around the west of Haydown Hill to Tidcombe, in the combined parish of
Tidcombe and Fosbury, where websites are also included here.
Oxenwood is in  Shalbourne parish further north.
Buttermere, the border parish north east of Fosbury ( north of Hampshire's Linkenholt and
Vernhams Dean ), is also represented by the Shalbourne category.
The western boundary of Chute parish is at Collingbourne Wood, represented
by  Collingbourne Ducis to the west.

1065209.title: Codford
1065209.description:
Codford is a parish south of Salisbury Plain, with its southern boundary on the River Wylye.
There is a linear settlement comprising Codford St Mary and Codford St Peter, which is
now bypassed by the A36 road between the villages and the river.
Downstream to the east, Wylye parish including Fisherton de la Mere is represented by  Steeple Langford east of the A303 road.
This category represents the parishes on the south bank of the Wylye, where a minor road bridges the Wylye to
Stockton to the south east and Sherrington to the south west.
The next parish upstream is Upton Lovell, before Knock, where the B390 road leads north east to  Chitterne
along the northern parish boundary over Codford Down, and from where Chitterne Brook flows
between Codford St Mary and Codford St Peter, before entering the Wylye.
Wilsbury Ring is at the top of Codford Hill, north east of the villages before East Codford Down,
and the eastern parish boundary with north of Wylye parish.

links.title: Take Thick with the Light
links.description: Project examining the connection between heritage, art and wellbeing through responding to a collection of letters from 1914-1917, by two brothers, George and Albert Stopher, whilst at Codford St Mary.

1063577.title: Colerne
1063577.description:
This category represents the parish of Colerne, which besides the village of this name, is home to RAF Colerne, and
stretches east to include hamlets of Eastrip and Thickwood before its eastern boundary on the west bank of By Brook.
To the east of the river are parishes of  Biddestone and  Corsham, with  Box to the south east and south.
The parish western boundary coincides with the unitary authority boundary with  South Gloucestershire at  Marshfield.
Upper and North Wraxhall are north of Doncombe Brook which forms the northern parish boundary
to Tatton Keynell to the north east.

1062319.title: Collingbourne Ducis
1062319.description:
Collingbourne Ducis is a village on the A338, taking road traffic south from  Burbage to  Tidworth in the south.
The A346 road leads to  Lugershall in the south east.
A minor road leads to  Everleigh in the west.
Collingbou­rne Wood is to the east separating the parish of  Chute, and the combined parish
of Tidcombe and Fosbury is to the north east.
This category also includes websites for the parish of Collingbou­rne Kingston immediately north of Collingbourne Ducis.

links.title: The Tipple Inn
links.description: Pub and restaurant. Profile, facilities, menu and gallery.

510791.title: Combe Bissett
510791.description:
Coombe Bissett is a village mainly on the south bank of the River Ebble, south west of  Salisbury on the A354 road to north Dorset.
Besides Coombe Bissett parish, this category lists websites for the parish upstream, Stratford Toney,
before  Bishopstone upstream to the west, and south to the Hampshire border at Whitsbury Down.
The small village of Homington down stream on the south bank of the Ebble is within
Coombe Bissett parish, before  Odstock to the east.

links.title: Combe Bissett
links.description: Local community website, with information on local services, facilities and events.

links.title: Linda Fripp Designs
links.description: Specialise in creating celebration cakes, using a variety of mediums. Profile, ordering, photographs, and contacts.

510819.title: Corsham
510819.description:
This category represents the parish of Corsham, which besides town of this name, stretches west
before Rudloe in the parish of  Box, and  Biddestone to the north.
The town is served by the A4 road and railway from  Chippenham in the north east.
Lacock is to the south east,  Atworth south of Corsham,
with  Melksham further to the south east.

links.title: Priory Street Baptist Church
links.description: Includes information about services, their location and a notice board.

links.title: Corsham Town Council
links.description: Providing information about councillors, meetings, local services and events in the town.

links.title: Corsham Court
links.description: A privately-owned historic house with a significant art collection, open to the visitors.  Site has details of opening times, access for disabled visitors, a garden diary, history and descriptions of the house, its contents and grounds - Corsham Park.

links.title: Corsham Cricket Club
links.description: Includes news, information, history, fixtures and results.

links.title: Corsham Festival
links.description: Annual arts festival.  Details of events and link to on-line booking service.

links.title: The Pound
links.description: Arts Centre offering performances, workshops, a Youth Theatre and exhibitions.  Details of forthcoming events and bookings.

links.title: Keltek Trust
links.description: Information about charity helping churches acquire surplus and/or redundant bells to be hung for English-style full-circle bell-ringing.

links.title: Corsham Civic Society
links.description: Organisation promoting the town, conservation and preservation. The site has a list of events, newsletters and information on specific projects.

links.title: Clove House
links.description: Family dentist offering NHS, general dentistry, dental implants and hygienist.

links.title: 1st Corsham Scout Group
links.description: Beavers, Cubs and Sea Scouts. News and contact information.

links.title: Corsham Amateur Swimming Club
links.description: News, club information, training and lesson times and a fixture list.

links.title: The Porch Surgery
links.description: The GP doctors surgery. Information about NHS and private clinics, contact details, surgery hours and news.

links.title: CMS Construction Consultants Ltd
links.description: Architectural services for design, construction and project management of mainly national developers. Services, projects and company history.

links.title: Clear Vision Accountancy Group
links.description: Chartered accountants also offering business advice and support. Tax and business advisory guides, search facility, and contact details.

links.title: Corsham Building Plastics
links.description: Suppliers and installers of windows, doors, conservatories, canopies, fascias, guttering. Description of the company, products, services and contact details.

links.title: Lucknam Park
links.description: Hotel with gourmet restaurant, spa, conference centre and equestrian centre. Includes pictures and descriptions of the facilities, tariff and location. [Colerne]

links.title: Quick Crepes
links.description: Mobile catering service. Details of functions provided for, menus and a quote page.

links.title: S & K Autos

links.title: Right Angle Picture Framing
links.description: A professional picture framing service.  Also an IT application - Wessex Pricing Program - which is used by picture framing businesses to calculate costs for framing work.

links.title: The English Group
links.description: Design agency. Information on the company's services including graphic and web design with portfolio of client projects.

links.title: Joyce Chanin Development Ltd
links.description: Provides services in house alterations, bespoke kitchens, house extensions and office fitting. [May not work in some browsers]

links.title: Crash Car Repairs
links.description: Provision of auto body and van repairs. Site includes information of services provided, gallery of work completed and customer testimonials.

links.title: Anka
links.description: Company specialising in the application of liquid metal finishes. Metal in a liquid form can be applied to a variety of substrates including, but not limited to wood, concrete, plaster, GRP and MDF.

links.description: Interior design, furniture and home shop. Profile, product range and services. [Corsham and Gastard]

links.description: Shopping centre. Profile and tenants.

links.description: Supplier of chemicals and biochemicals, including antibiotics diagnostics reagents for scientific and pharmaaceutocal industries. Includes safety documentation, and global distribution contacts.

1008632.title: Travel and Tourism
1008632.description: This category includes sites for area attractions and resources for those travelling in the town, including tourist guides.

links.title: Park Farm Barn
links.description: Bed and breakfast accommodation. Includes information, photographs and contact details.

links.title: Church Farm
links.description: Farmhouse bed and breakfast at Hartham. Describes facilities and accommodation. Prices, photographs and contacts.

links.title: Corsham Area Heritage
links.description: Providing information on the town including, forthcoming events, local attractions, newsletter and contact details.

1065096.title: Corsley
1065096.description:
Corsley is civil parish north west of  Warminster, with it major conurbation
Corsley Heath on the A632 road to  Frome.
The settlements of Dertfords, Lane End and Lye's Green are on the boundary with  Somerset Mendips.
Longhedge, Whitbourne Moor are south of the A632, before the boundary of Longleat Safari Park,
which stretches into  Horningsham parish to the south.
Sturford and Cley Hill are on the eastern boundary, before  Longbridge Deverill parish to the south east.
Corsley is a relatively small village north of the A632, before Huntenbull Green in 
Chapmanslade parish on the A3098 road further north.

links.title: Longleat House and Safari Park
links.description: An Elizabethan stately home set in a park which became the first safari park outside Africa. Details of opening times and attractions, with photographs and other visitor information.

links.title: Tea and Sympathy
links.description: Catering business specialising in after the funeral service, providing crockery, cutlery and flowers. Includes sample menus, gallery, testimonials, and contacts.

510789.title: Corston
510789.description:
Corston is a small village on the A429 road south of the town of  Malmesbury in the civil parish of
St Paul Malmesbury Without, which surrounds the town, south of  Brokenborough to the north west.
Websites for Burton Hill just south of the Sherston branch of the River Avon are listed with the town,
as are those for Milbourne immediately east of the town in St Paul Malmesbury Without.
Besides Corston, this category lists websites for the hamlet of Rodbourne to the south east, as
well as Rodbourne Bottom south of the railway, before  Great Somerford.
Lower Stanton St Quintin is next south on the A429, east of Hullavington Airfield, represented by  Hullavington.
Norton is the parish west of St Paul Malmesbury Without, which doesn't have an elected
parish council, but holds an annual Parish meeting.
Access is best from Hullavington, so websites for south east of  Sherston are listed there.

links.title: Analogue Integration
links.description: Services and products offered by electronic consultants.

links.title: Creative Business Solutions
links.description: A consultancy with expertise in delivering creativity and innovation projects. Also specialise in training and development activities in related areas.

510752.title: Cricklade
510752.description:
Cricklade is a town and Wiltshire Council parish, north west of the Swindon AU's villages of  Blunsdon St Andrew
and Broad Blunsdon, from where the A419 road bypasses the north of the town on the way to  Cirencester.
Cricklade can be considered the first town on the  River Thames, which flows from
Cotswold Water Park in  Ashton Keynes, north of the town westwards through Latton parish,
then the Swindon unitary authority parish of  Castle Eaton.

links.title: Cricklade Hotel and Country Club
links.description: Information about accommodation with golf course and swimming pool. Also hosts wedding receptions and conferences.

links.title: Friends of St Mary's Church
links.description: History and development, contact details, press cuttings, and marriage registers from the 17th century.

links.title: Cricklade and District Twinning Association
links.description: Twinned with the town of Suce sur Erdre in France, includes details of events as well as providing background and links for both towns.

links.title: Cricklade in Bloom
links.description: Information about Cricklade Bloomers a volunteer group working to improve Cricklade and enter the RHS Britain in Bloom competition. Includes details of North Meadow National Nature Reserve home of 80% of the UK population of Snakes Head Fritillaries.

links.title: Cricklade Dental Practice
links.description: Information about treatments, appointments, location and staff profiles.

links.title: Cricklade Model Flying Club
links.description: Presents news and membership information, including designs for model turbines.

links.title: Loadpoint Ltd.
links.description: Company and product information for manufacturers of high precision dicing, scribing and grinding machines, and air-bearing spindles.

links.title: mLettings
links.description: Letting agent. Provides details of properties available, information for tenants and landlords, client references and contact information.

links.title: Pensions and Annuities Ltd.
links.description: Annuities and annuity quotes from Independent Financial Advisers.

links.title: Thamesdown Recycling
links.description: Provides profile with details of services.

510817.title: Crudwell
510817.description:
Crudwell is a village and north Wiltshire parish, on the A439 which takes road traffic past Cotswold Airport,
before the boundary with the  Cotswold district of Gloucestershire, at  Kemble.
The hamlets of Chelworth and Eastcourt are within the parish before  Oaksey to the east.
Upper Minety is next to the south east, and is within the parish of  Minety.
Hankerton parish is directly south where websites are listed in the  Charlton category.
The western parish boundary is with the  Cotswold district of Gloucestershire at Long Newton,
and  Brokenborough is on the boundary to the south west.

links.title: Richardson Event Hire
links.description: Company information and details of hire for special occasions, corporate and sporting events.

links.title: The  Rectory
links.description: Information about country house hotel situated in three acres of gardens.

links.title: Crudwell Village Hall
links.description: Photographs, event program and contact details for this community resource.

1059539.title: Dauntsey
1059539.description:
This category lists websites for the Wiltshire parish of Dauntsey; Dauntsey Vale east
of  Great and Little Somerford to  Brinkworth north of the M4 motorway.
Grittenham is south of the M4 motorway, and is within Brinkworth parish.
Besides Dauntsey, this category includes websites for the parish of Tockenham, where the northern
boundary is with Grittenham around the railway line, with  Royal Wootton Bassett to the north east.
Clyffe Pypard is next village to the south east of Tockenham, which with Broad Town parish,
is represented by  Broad Hinton further east.
Clyffe Pypard parish extends along the southern boundary of Tockenham parish to Hilmarton parish,
which is south on the A3102 road, south of  Lyneham, which is south of the
Dauntsey parish boundary at Bradenstoke.
The hamlet of Dauntsey Lock is south of the railway, and Sodom is between this and
the M4 motorway west of Dauntsey's eastern parish boundary west of Grittenham.
The B4069 road leads south west between the railway and motorway to  Christian Malford
is west of the parish boundary.
This boundary follows the course of a dismantled branch of the railway to the River Avon
where the bridge connects the parishes of Dauntsey and Great Somerford.
North of Daunstey House and Park, Somerford Bridge over Brinkworth Brook links Daunstey
and Little Somerford, before it forms the northern boundary with Brinkworth.

links.title: Dauntsey Wiltshire
links.description: Community information, introducing the parish council, church, history, the doom board, school, amenities, clubs, organisations, businesses, newletter archive, notices and contacts.

510830.title: Devizes
510830.description:
This category lists websites for the market town and Wiltshire parish of Devizes.
North west of the town, the A342 road from  Chippenham, enters the town via  Rowde.
The A342 continues through the town, leading east to  Upavon, via the parishes of Stert and  Urchfont,
with Urchfont village to the south, villages of Wedhampton, Chirton and Wilsford to the north,
with Marden parish, where websites are listed in the Urchfont category.
The A361 road from  Avebury in the north east, enters the locality from  Bishops Cannings,
via Roundway parish where websites are included with Devizes.
South of Devizes the A360 road to Salisbury leads south through  Potterne,  West Lavington,
  Tilshead,  Shrewton, before  Winterbourne Stoke.
The A365 road leads west from the town to  Seend and  Melksham.

links.title: Devizes Town Council
links.description: A guide for visitors and residents. Basic information on the council, plus events information and a local services directory.

links.title: St James' Southbroom
links.description: Information from the parish church for the eastern half of the town.

links.title: Devizes & District Wargames Group
links.description: DDWG covers historical/fantasy wargames, role playing and collectable card games.

links.title: Devizes Volleyball Club
links.description: Information about this club for both juniors and adults.

links.title: St Andrew's Church
links.description: Joint Methodist and United Reformed church offers minister, plans, purpose, worship and activities.

links.title: Devizes Photography Club
links.description: Details of meetings, membership and newsletter.

links.title: Devizes
links.description: Describes this town and its facilities with tourist information, events and history.

links.title: Devizes Rugby Football Club
links.description: Teams, fixtures, results and illustrated match reports, league tables, news and rolling Diary of events, for 3 Senior teams plus Tag, Mini/Midi and Youth rugby.

links.title: White Horse Yoga Centre
links.description: Offers one to one yoga teaching or group classes, including therapy, pregnancy and somatics meditation. Time table for workshops and courses, FAQ, team profile and contacts at Roundway.

510833.title: Arts and Entertainment
510833.description: This category includes sites about local artistic, cultural and entertainment activities, events, institutions, businesses and organisations.

links.title: Bluestone Gallery
links.description: Describes a local art gallery, includes photo tour of a selection of the items on display, location and contact details.

links.title: Devizes Chamber Choir
links.description: An amateur choir with no entry audition performing three concerts a year.

510835.title: Business and Economy
510835.description: This category includes sites covering the business and economic activities of the town, including listings of most companies and industries.

links.title: PJ Dyke Paving and Groundworks
links.description: Specialises in driveways, hard landscaping and small civil engineering works. Pictures of completed jobs, testimonials and contact information.

links.title: Dibtech Computers
links.description: Product and service list with prices, contact details and a message board.

links.title: Rangebourne Petcare
links.description: Information on the independent pet shop, and the services they offer.

links.title: Mike Wood Tyres Ltd
links.description: Supply and fit tyres exhausts and batteries. Includes opening times, location and tyre tips.

links.title: Moore of Devizes
links.description: A company offering heating installation services for commercial and domestic clients. Also offers electrical, plumbing and air conditioning installations.

links.title: Estcourt Vets
links.description: Services for dogs, cats, rabbits, other small pet care plus farm animal and horse visits. Includes facility information, news, hours of service and staff profiles.

links.title: Macqueen Veterinary Centre
links.description: Orthopaedic referral service for small animals. Provides details of diagnosis services and treatments offered.

links.title: Avon Trophies

links.title: AKC

links.title: Catleys Gas Centre
links.description: Supply, installation and service of gas appliances, Calor gas and air products and an autogas refuelling station.

links.title: The Fire Alarm Consultancy Limited
links.description: Design, installation, service and maintenance specialists in fire alarms, emergency lighting and nurse call systems for the private, commercial and industrial sectors.

links.title: Goodman Nash Ltd.
links.description: Dedicated business rates and property audit company serving corporate or SME, aiming to discover and recover overpayments. Profile with history, experience, technology and team, with contacts for local head office and Bristol.

510834.title: Education
510834.description: Includes local educational institutions, programmes and opportunities; as well as other location specific educational resources.
