510678.description: This category includes sites about local government, policing, judicial system, taxation and the military.

links.title: Melksham Town Council
links.description: Providing event information, town map, history, council and places of interest. Business, organisations and general information is also included together with contact details.

510682.title: Health
510682.description: Includes health and medical resources specific to the town.

links.title: Spa Medical Centre
links.description: Describes the practice and its services with information about opening times and making appointments.

links.title: Haine and Smith
links.description: Family run opticians with several practices throughout Wiltshire. Site includes information on eye care, services provided, offers available and patient feedback.

links.title: Giffords Surgery
links.description: Information on the clinic, doctors, nursing staff and the services provided. Also includes health information and details for new patients.

links.title: Melksham Chiropractic Clinic
links.description: Providing details on therapies provided and pain management. Also includes frequently asked questions section and treatment fees.

links.title: Watson's Court Health Clinic
links.description: Chiropractic clinic, also specialising in holistic therapies and biomechanics. Site provides overview of the clinic and services on offer.

510679.title: Recreation and Sports
510679.description: Recreational and sporting clubs and activities open to residents of Melksham.

links.title: Spencer Melksham Bowls Club
links.description: Outdoor and indoor bowls. Meeting times, prices and club information.

510684.title: Society and Culture
510684.description: This category includes sites that reflect the make up of the town's community: its people, its history, and resources and institutions that serve the town's people, such as social service organisations.

links.title: Save the Train
links.description: A campaign to improve rail services for Melksham.  Includes statistics, background materials, news and commentary.

links.title: Queensway Chapel
links.description: Evangelical church, information about services, pastoral care, activities and regular newsletter.

510685.title: Religion
510685.description: This category lists sites for the community's religious institutions, organisations and resources.

links.title: Melksham Baptist Church
links.description: Photo gallery, contacts and club information.

510683.title: Transport
510683.description: This category includes sites providing area transport resources for those travelling to and from, and within the town.

510680.title: Travel and Tourism
510680.description: Bed & Breakfast and hotels in the Melksham area.

links.title: Well House Manor
links.description: Business accommodation and conference facilities. Photographs and online availability.

links.title: Beechfield House Hotel
links.description: Accommodation and facilities described with room rates. Photo gallery and contacts at Beanacre.

links.title: Great Chalfield Manor
links.description: National Trust historic home. Profile and facilities with information about private functions.

510762.title: Mere
510762.description:
Mere is a small market town in south west Wiltshire, separated from South Somerset by  Zeals.
The town is now bypassed to the north by the A303 trunk road, on the way to  Wincanton.
Mere Down is to the north of the A303 before  Kingston Deverill.
West Knoyle before Mere parish extends south west of the town along the Dorset border
at  Silton, Milton on Stour and  Motcombe, to  Sedghill and Semley.

links.title: Yapp Brothers Ltd.
links.description: Wine merchants present available wines, with food pairing advice and online sales,

links.title: Country Weddings Flowers
links.description: Includes services offered and a gallery of previous floristry undertaken, with contacts for consultations by appointment.

links.title: Castleton House
links.description: Family bed and breakfast accommodation with off street parking and outdoor heated swimming pool. Details of local attractions, interior photographs, rates, availability link, and booking contacts.

links.title: Mere Amateur Dramatic Society
links.description: Also incorporates the literary festival. Meeting dates, history of the society, details of past and future productions, with link to social media.

links.title: Mere Library
links.description: Information on services and volunteer operated opening hours.

1064965.title: Minety
1064965.description:
Minety is a village and north Wiltshire parish, which includes the village of Upper Minety.
North of the railway line from Swindon, the hamlet of Lower Moor is before the county boundary
with Neigh Bridge Country Park in the  Cotswolds district of Gloucestershire.
Oaksey is to the north west, and Hankerton to the west is represented by  Charlton.
Brinkworth is next south, and Braydon a small parish to the east is represented by the  Purton.
Websites for Leigh parish are included in the  Ashton Keynes category.

links.title: Minety Rugby Football Club
links.description: Includes club details, officers and photographs.

510863.title: Monkton Farleigh
510863.description:
This category represents the parish of Monkton Farleigh, which is north west of  Bradford-on-Avon on the
A363 road, on the unitary authority boundary with  Bath & NES at  Claverton, south of  Bathford.
The parish is north of  Winsley high above the east of the River Avon, under which the Bath stone
has been mined, and served as a World War 2 Ministry of Defence underground ammunition store.
Besides Monkton Farleigh village north of the A363, the hamlets of Farleigh Wick and Pinckney Green are on the A363.
Kingsdown is north of the parish boundary in  Box parish.
South Wraxall is to the east.

links.title: Monkton Farleigh Parish Council
links.description: Information of the community's administration, with records of meetings, policies and finances. Virtual tour of the centre, cdetails of village hall, organisations, events, newsblog and contacts.

links.title: Monkton Farleigh Osteopathic Practice
links.description: State registered with the General Osteopathic Council, offering a broad range of specialisms including paediatrics, sports injuries and chronic pain. overview of treatments, news blog, opening times and contacts.

510676.title: Netheravon
510676.description:
Netheravon is the village in the middle of Salisbury Plain, on the A345 road, north of  Durrington.
Besides the parish of Netheravon, this category represents the surrounding rural area, including
the parishes of Figheldean to the south, Fittleton cum Haxton to the east,
Enford to the north, and Orcheston to the west.

links.title: Cafe Guate
links.description: Family business offering product sales and charter of a mobile coffee shop.

links.title: RGV Engineering
links.description: Business offering plumbing, heating and electrical services and contracting.

links.title: Army Parachute Association
links.description: Skydiving courses for both military and the general public.

links.title: Netheravon Online
links.description: News and local information for Netheravon, Fittleton, Haxton and surrounding area.

510808.title: Nettleton
510808.description:
Nettleton is the parish on the South Gloucestershire boundary coinciding with the M4 motorway,
which is bridged by the B4039 road over to  Acton Turville from the village of Burton.
From Burton, the B4039 continues east to The Gibb, then south east to the parish of  Castle Combe.
This category also includes websites for North Wraxhall also on the South Gloucestershire
boundary, north of the A420 road to  Marshfield.

510704.title: News and Media
510704.description: Sites about local magazines, radio and television stations, newspapers and similar media in Wiltshire.

links.title: BBC Wiltshire
links.description: The BBC site for the county with news, sport, music, clubbing, and views.

links.title: The Wiltshire Gazette & Herald
links.description: Includes news, sports, leisure activities, schools, businesses and other local resources.

links.title: Heart Wiltshire
links.description: Adult contemporary radio station. Features schedules, presenter profiles, showbiz and music news. Available on FM, DAB and live web stream.

links.title: Wiltshire Times
links.description: Regulary updated news and information covering the county.

510777.title: Nomansland
510777.description:
Nomansland is the boundary village at the south east tip of Wiltshire Council,
with Hampshire at Bramshaw, within the parish of  Landford.
This category lists websites for the northern tip of the New Forest National Park, which show
addresses south of Langford Common, but includes Hamptworth Common and Franchises Wood.
Burnt Ground Wood is in  Redlynch parish, where the southern border area
is represented by the  Woodfalls.

links.title: The New Forest Church of England Primary School
links.description: The local Church of England Primary School educating Key Stage 2 children from the area surrounding the South Wiltshire villages of Landford, Nomansland and Hamptworth.

1065211.title: North Wraxall
1065211.description:
North Wraxall is the Wiltshire parish on the A420 road from  Chippenham before crossing
the unitary authority boundary with South Gloucestershire at Marshfield.
North Wraxall is a village just north of the A420, and Upper Wraxall is the
last hamlet before the boundary, with The Shoe on the A420 before that.
Mountain Bower is on the north west boundary with  Nettleton.
Ford in on the A420 at the eastern boundary with  Castle Combe to the north east,
and  Biddestone to the south east. 
Colerne is the parish on the western boundary with Marshfield to the south.
Note: South Wraxall is a separate parish, which with the hamlet of Lower Wraxall is represented by  Monkton Farleigh.  
Besides Wiltshire, the name Wraxall is shared with parishes in Dorset and Somerset, having derived from the Saxon: "nook of land frequented by the buzzard or other bird of prey".[ https://bafhs.org.uk/wraxall/?v=79cba1185463 ]

links.title: North Wraxall Parish Council
links.description: Admintration covering a community of five villages and hamlets with records of meetings, finances, planning, notices, contacts, photographs, amenities and related links.

links.title: North Wraxall Parish
links.description: Introduction to the area, its village and hamlets, with photo gallery. Information about St James church, the community hall, events, clubs and societies.

links.title: Delomosne
links.description: Fine antique glass and porcelain on view by appointment at theirthe showroom in North Wraxall.

510818.title: Oaksey
510818.description:
Oaksey is a village and north Wiltshire parish, on the county boundary with Poole Keynes and
Neigh Bridge Country Park represented by  Somerford Keynes.
Chelworth is a hamlet to the west, in the parish of  Crudwell.
Hankerton parish is directly south, represented by  Charlton.
The parish of  Minety is to the south east.

links.title: Oaksey Park Golf
links.description: A 9 hole golf course situated on the Oaksey Park and Leisure Estate. Clubhouse, course, functions, corporate days, competitions, events, directions, and contacts.

links.title: Oaksey Cricket Club
links.description: News, results, fixtures, and club information.

links.title: Oaksey Village
links.description: Parish news, diary, links and details of local services and amenities.

1064956.title: Oare
1064956.description:
Oare is a small village on the A345 road north of  Pewsey from  Marlborough.
The village of Wilcot is south west of Oare, to the west of the A345, spanning the Kennet and Avon Canal.
The village of Huish is north west of Oare, and since May 2021, these have been administered as the
combined parish of Wilcot, Huish and Oare, which this category represents.
Clench Common to the north east on the A345 is in  Savernake parish.
Wootton Rivers parish directly east is represented by the Savernake category.
Wootton Rivers village is on the north bank of the canal, whereas websites for
Milton Lilbourne south of the canal are included with Pewsey.

links.title: Blakeney Interiors
links.description: Product details, links and contact information.

1062326.title: Odstock
1062326.description:
Odstock is a village on the south bank of the River Ebble, downstream from  Coombe Bissett, south of Britford.
Nunton village is downstream before the A338 road within Odstock parish, south from  Salisbury.
The hamlet of Bodenham is east of the A338 before the eastern parish boundary on the River Avon.
Downton is directly south.

links.title: Kismet Photography
links.description: Photographers specialising in wedding, boudoir, commercial and early years. Includes portfolio and information on their services.

510827.title: Ogbourne
510827.description:
This category represents the parishes of Ogbourne St Andrew & Ogbourne St George, administered by Wiltshire Council,
north of  Marlborough on the A346 towards  Swindon.
The next parish to the east is  Aldbourne, and the Marlborough Downs extend to the west.

links.title: Ogbourne CofE Primary School
links.description: Aims, staff, governors, term dates, events, news, and admissions.

links.title: Silks On The Downs
links.description: Pub and restaurant also offering accommodation. Menus, accommodation details and includes a virtual tour.

510798.title: Pewsey
510798.description:
Pewsey is the largest settlement in the Vale of Pewsey, east of  Devizes.
The Vale of Pewsey lies between the the Marlborough Downs and Salisbury Plain.
Pewsey is served by a railway station on the Reading to Taunton line, and the
Kennet and Avon Canal, flows through the north of Pewsey parish.
Pewsey Down at the south of the parish features Pewsey White Horse, cut in 1937,
to replace one existing since the eighteenth century.
To the south, Abbots and Bruce Downs are in the southern extremes of  Manningfold parish,
south west of Pewsey, and  Everleigh parish is to the south east.
Milton Hill is to the east, in Milton Lilbourne parish, for which websites are also included here.
Milton Lilbourne parish stretches over the canal to the north, where the boundary is
with Wootton Rivers represented by  Savernake further north east.
The A345 road leads north from Pewsey to  Marlborough first passing through the combined parish of  Wilcot, Huish and Oare.
Wilcot village is on the canal west of Pewsey, before  Woodborough parish and  Honeystreet.

links.title: British Forces Foundation
links.description: Information about events and fundraising for charity which organises entertainment to raise the morale of British forces serving overseas. The Chairman of the charity's Trustees is performer Jim Davidson.

links.title: Pewsey Village Website
links.description: History, photo gallery and services available in and around the village.

links.title: Pewsey Methodist Church
links.description: Includes services, news and activities.

links.title: Pewsey Vale Amateur Dramatic Society
links.description: Events, information about their latest show, list of members, newsletters, reviews and photographs.

links.title: Johnny Hawkes
links.description: Portfolio and contact details for commissioned and product-based furniture by artist and engineer in wood, metal and plastics.

links.title: Manningford Croft
links.description: Estate agents offering sales and lettings in the Pewsey Vale and Marlborough area, listing property details, online submission to their mailing list, and contacts for office.

links.title: Curl Up & Dye Hair Studio
links.description: Offering free consultation with a fresh mocha or herbal tea either in the bustling studio or their courtyard. Profile, care range, photo gallery, pricing, opening times, contacts and location.

links.title: St Francis School
links.description: Independent school for pupils aged 2-13. Includes term calendar, history and department pages.

links.title: Pewsey Primary School
links.description: For children aged 4 to 11. Prospectus, pupil's work, newsletters and residential visits.

links.title: Pewsey Vale School
links.description: Details of learning for pupils aged 11-16. Includes governance, policies, curriculum, staff, diary, and facilities available for hire.

links.title: Pewsey Vale Running Club
links.description: Concentrates on road, marathon and cross country running.

links.title: Pewsey Heritage Centre
links.description: A Wiltshire museum dedicated to the history of Pewsey Vale.

510803.title: Pitton
510803.description:
Pitton is a village between the A30 and A36 east of  Salisbury.
The village of  Farley is directly south, and is administered as the combined parish of Pitton and Farley.
West Dean parish separates Farley and Pitton from the Hampshire boundary.
The parish of  Winterslow is north on this boundary, and  Firsdown is immediately north.
The parish of Clarendon Park is directly west, and websites for this area may be included here.

links.title: The Silver Plough
links.description: Public House, has menu and drinks list as well as information on the pub and its owners.

510690.title: Porton
510690.description:
Porton is a village on the A338 in the parish of   Idmiston, north of  Winterbourne Gunner
and south of  Allington and Boscombe.
This category includes websites for Gomeldon which was a medieval villageon the east bank of the source of the River Bourne.
The conurbation now extends west of the valley and the A338, West Gomeldon and east of the railway, East Gomeldon, where Idmiston's southern boundary extends up Porton Down.
This category also lists websites for the area east of the railway from Porton village extending up Idmiston Down,
before Easton Down in  Winterslow to the south east.

links.title: Defence Scientific and Technical Laboratory
links.description: Provides advice and technical support to the Ministry of Defence on science and technology issues. Information on careers opportunities, products and services offered. Located at Porton Down.

links.title: Ploughshare Innovations Ltd.
links.description: Manages technology transfer on behalf of the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory. Profile, technologies, news, events, and contacts. Located at Porton Down.

510785.title: Potterne
510785.description:
Potterne is a village and Wiltshire Council parish on the A360 road south from  Devizes,
before continuing through  Littleton Panell, over Salisbury Plain via  Tilshead.
Potterne Wick is a hamlet before the eastern boundary with  Urchfont parish to the east.
Worton is to the south west.
A minor road leads to Caen Hill to the north west.
Poulshot is the next parish north west.

links.title: Stable Cottage
links.description: Offers self-catering holiday accommodation in a thatched 17th century cottage. Includes photographs, prices and testimonials.

links.title: Twigs Crafts
links.description: Hand-made decorations and gifts inspired by folk art, incorporating homespun fabrics, herbs and spices.  Includes an illustrated product catalogue and home project ideas.

links.title: Potterne Cricket Club
links.description: Formed in 1936 with its home on the southern side of the village. Fixtures, results, club history, constitution, social events and merchandise.

links.title: PKA Architects Ltd.
links.description: A practice undertaking all building forms, but especially housing, equestrian, small commercial projects and sustainable design. Portfolio and history.

links.title: White Horse Computer Training
links.description: Computer training and support in the Wiltshire area for home and business. Course outlines and service details.

links.title: M Godding Ltd
links.description: Specialising  in  rare, out-of-print and other hard-to-find books including many first edition prints. Online shop, catalogue browser and search, valuation and repair service details.

links.title: Music Workshop
links.description: Peter Lamb's sound recording studio and location recording services. List of projects, session musicians, secondhand instruments.

links.title: Blounts Court Farm
links.description: Bed and breakfast accommodation. Includes prices, location details and photographs.

links.title: Potterne Young Learners’ Partnership
links.description: Community information for Carers Nest Pre-School based next to Five Lanes Primary School. Profile, contacts, job vacancies, and related Links.

links.title: Facebook: Potterne Parish Council
links.description: Agenda and minutes, councillor details, planning applications and awards.

links.title: Wellsprings Benefice
links.description: Church of England community that worships together across five churches in the parishes of Bulkington, Potterne, Poulshot, Seend and Worton and Marston.

links.title: Inner Space
links.description: Interior design in contemporary and traditional style. Includes contact details and images of work.

1065197.title: Poulshot
1065197.description:
Poulshot is a Wiltshire Council parish south of the Kennet and Avon Canal between  Seend and  Devizes.
The A361 road crosses the north of the parish, from which Poulshot village is south,
and the hamlet of Townsend is south west before  Worton to the south.
Potterne is the parish to the east.

links.title: Poulshot Nurseries
links.description: Wholesale supplier of plants to the trade. Profile, brochure, with photos of top species, varieties and availability list, and contacts.

510807.title: Purton
510807.description:
Purton is a parish administered by Wiltshire Council, north west of  Swindon.
Lydiard Millicent is directly south, sharing the same eastern unitary authority boundary,
which coincides with the River Ray.
The north west parishes of Swindon are represented by the  Blunsdon category.
Cricklade is directly north and Purton parish includes Purton Stoke before this boundary.
The Swindon and Cricklade railway has a station at Hayes Knoll on the east of the parish.
Besides these, this category also lists websites for Braydon parish to the west,
before  Minety to the north west, and  Brinkworth to the south west.

links.title: Kemdent
links.description: Supply specialist dental materials. Includes product descriptions and special offers.

links.title: The Pear Tree
links.description: Details of facilities at small country house hotel and restaurant with two rosettes. Includes 360 degree panoramic photographs.

links.title: Bradon Forest School
links.description: Fundraising information and prospectus for comprehensive school.

links.title: Swindon Loft Conversions Ltd
links.description: Specialists in converting lofts or attic space into extra rooms. General information, photographs, and contacts.

links.title: Byrne & King Ltd
links.description: Contractor offering construction, groundwork and plant hire. Profile and services with career information.

links.title: Biocraft South West
links.description: Damp proofing and basement conversion specialists. Serving the South West, covering Bath, Bristol, Chippenham, Marlborough and Swindon.

links.title: Purton Museum and Historical Society
links.description: Representing 2,000 years of the village's history from the Ringsbury Camp Iron Age Hillfort, through Roman and Saxon finds towards the present day. With museum catalogue, events and courses.

510779.title: Ramsbury
510779.description:
Ramsbury is a village and parish administered by Wiltshire Council, 4 miles east of  Marlborough, on the north bank of the River Kennet.
Chilton Foliat parish is directly east on the north bank, before the unitary authority boundary with West Berkshire at  Hungerford.
A bridge connects Ramsbury village with the parish of  Froxfield south of the River Kennet, and along the north bank to the west is the linear settlement of Axford.
Websites for these areas are included here, whereas websites for the area further west, in the parish of Mildenhall are included under the Marlborough category.
Websites for the area to the north west in the parishes of Ogbourne St Andrew & Ogbourne St George,
are listed together in the  Ogbourne category.
The parish of  Albourne is directly north, and to the north east
the parish extends to  Baydon.

links.title: Ramsbury at War
links.description: A short history of the village and its airfield from 1939-1945 by Roger Day.

links.title: Fairfax Properties Ltd
links.description: Provides a service in the design and construction of bespoke classically styled country houses.

links.title: Ramsbury
links.description: This Wikipedia encyclopaedia entry describes the village.

links.title: Fat Birder Wiltshire
links.description: Top sites for birdwatching in the county, resources and links.

links.title: The Wiltshire Volleyball Association
links.description: News, rules, fixtures and results, tables, pictures and club details.

links.title: Barbury International Horse Trials
links.description: International horse trials at Barbury Castle, featuring show jumping, cross country and dressage with information for spectators, riders, hospitality and sponsorship including event videos, news and results.

links.title: Wiltshire Squash Rackets Association
links.description: Club details, summer and winter leagues, cup competition and player rankings.

510710.title: Football
510710.description: This category deals with football associations, leagues, clubs, teams, and coaching.

510709.title: Walking
510709.description: These sites contain information and walks for those who wish to explore the county on foot.

links.title: Foot Trails
links.description: Offers guided walking breaks in Wiltshire.

links.title: Wansdyke
links.description: This site describes its course, with maps and how to get there.

links.title: Wiltshire Walks
links.description: Provides relaxed guided walks around the woods, downs and ancient sites of Wiltshire.

510856.title: Redlynch
510856.description:
Redlynch is a village and parish east of  Downton.  The B3080 takes road traffic from Downton
though the old village, then south through  Woodfalls to the Hampshire border at Hale.
Whereas this category lists websites for Morgan's Vale, the conurbation that continues west of the old village,
the hamlet of Bohemia and village of Lover east of the B3080 along the boundary are represented by the Woodfalls category.
East of Redlynch village, Redlynch parish extends to the northern tip of the New Forest National Park, which separates  Landford to the east.
A minor road leads north of the forest to  Whiteparish further north east.

1064998.title: Rowde
1064998.description:
Rowde is a village east of the A342, from  Chippenham, directly north west of  Devizes.
Rowde parish includes the hamlet of Tanis to the east of the village,
before Roundway parish to the east where websites are included with Devizes.
Bromham parish is on the northern boundary, and Bromham village is on the A342 north west of the village.
Seend is to the west and before the southern boundary with Devizes and Poulshot parish,
the Kennet and Avon Canal featuring the flight of 16 locks is at Caen Hill.

links.title: Foxhangers Ltd.
links.description: Offers boating holidays on the Kennet and Avon canal. Pricing, availability, photographs, map and contacts west of Caen Hill Locks.

links.title: Wikipedia: Caen Hill Locks
links.description: Article on the 29 locks west of Sells Green, rising of 72 metres in 2 miles (1:44 gradient) in three groups; the lower seven locks, Foxhangers Wharf Lock to Foxhangers Bridge Lock, before sixteen locks scheduled monument. History, restoration photographs, plan, references and related links.

510729.title: Salisbury
510729.description: City and market town on the edge of Salisbury Plain, 135 km southwest of London . Population approximately 40000, an agricultural centre, and industries include brewing and engineering.   The cathedral of St Mary, built 1220/58, an example of Early English architecture; its spire at 123 m/404 ft is the highest in England. The cathedral library contains one of only four copies of the Magna Carta.   Situated at the confluence of four rivers, Salisbury is the only city within the county of Wiltshire .

links.title: Salisbury Journal
links.description: Includes news, sports, leisure activities, schools, businesses and other local resources.

links.title: Salisbury City Council
links.description: Information on council services. Including, local amenities, news, upcoming events, list of local councillors and contact details.

510734.title: Arts and Entertainment
510734.description: This category includes sites about local artistic, cultural and entertainment activities, events, institutions, businesses and organisations.

links.title: The Salisbury Project
links.description: A photographic archive of the Cathedral, town, and parish churches, provided by the McIntire Department of Art, University of Virginia, directed by Marion Roberts.

links.title: Salisbury Festival
links.description: A multi disciplinary arts organisation located throughout the city. Provides information on events and locations .

links.title: The Wardrobe
links.description: Regimental museum for the Royal Gloucestershire, Berkshire and Wiltshire Regiment. Offers information on the regiments, history, collections, and visitor guides.

links.title: Studio Theatre
links.description: Amateur drama group provides information on the theatre, history, news and reviews, past and future productions, and membership.

links.title: Music in Salisbury
links.description: An annual celebration of classical music with events throughout the year. Offers information on programme, performers, composers, and local community links.

links.title: Salisbury and South Wiltshire Museum
links.description: Home of the Stonehenge gallery . Includes photographs of the gallery and offers information on current events, facilities, location and membership .

links.title: Salisbury Guildhall
links.description: Entertainment, conference and wedding venue. Contains information on rooms, facilities and charges.

links.title: Salisbury Sinfonia
links.description: Chamber Orchestra. Has an overview of orchestra and upcoming events.

links.title: Sarum Voices
links.description: Local young choir. Information on the choir, its members and their events.

links.title: Royal School of Church Music
links.description: Educational Christian charity promoting best use of music in worship. Training schemes, online shop, and events throughout England.

links.title: St.John Singers
links.description: The Choir exists to sing services in cathedrals and churches and to support different national and local charities through its concerts. Includes history and programme of events.

links.title: Salisbury Community Choir
links.description: Information on the choir and their history as well as details of upcoming events and rehearsals.

links.title: The Sarum Consort
links.description: Vocal ensemble. Profile, upcoming concerts and CDs for sale.

510740.title: Business and Economy
510740.description: Includes sites covering the business and economic activities of the City and it's localities .

links.title: Endell Vets
links.description: Veterinary service for farm animals, equine clinic and domestic pets, including diagnostic, surgical and medical facilities. Offers information on services, opening times, location and a children's fun page.

links.title: Marie Mills
links.description: Counsellor, includes information on services and details of qualifications and experience.

links.title: John H Mitchell
links.description: Electrical contractor servicing domestic, industrial, commercial and agricultural sectors.

links.title: Guitar Repairs UK
links.description: Luthier, Specialises in making and repairing steel string acoustic guitars. Has information on the services and prices.

links.title: Selmech
links.description: Manufacture and distribute forage applicators for, grass and maize silage, grain crimping, and wholecrop silage. Includes product photographs and information on fitting and installation.

links.title: Jas Hair
links.description: Hair and beauty salon. Information on their services, products and jobs.

links.title: Venus and Mars
links.description: Beauty salon offer a range of beauty treatments, information on services, testimonials and the company.

links.title: Naim Audio
links.description: Design and manufacture a range of audio equipment. Provide both technical and standard user product information, a factory tour and FAQs, discussion forum and a shop.

links.title: Maidment and Carter Limited
links.description: Builders. List of services provided, customer testimonials, gallery of previous work undertaken and contact details.

links.title: Salisbury Printing
links.description: Print and design company specialising in litho & digital printing. Information on their services, facilities and a portfolio.

links.title: The Washing Well
links.description: Launderette in the centre of the city, offering serviced and self-service facilities. Information on prices, services and location.

510822.title: Savernake
510822.description:
Savernake is the forest immediately south east of  Marlborough, and this category lists
websites for the privately owned estate and the surrounding civil parish.
The hamlet of Cadley is on the A346 road, on the western edge of Savernake Forest,
before Burbage Common and the Kennet and Avon Canal in  Burbage parish.
The remains of Savernake railway stations are south of Durley, from when the Marlborough line ran north west, and west of Cadley.
The parish of Wootton Rivers is south and west of the course of this railway, and Wootton Top Lock, was formerly known as Cadley Lock.
Wootton Rivers village is on the north bank of canal, and websites for Wootton Rivers parish are included here.
Websites for Milton Lilbourne are included with  Pewsey further south west.
Oare is further west, on the A345, south west of the Savernake hamlet of Clench Common.
Manton to the north west is in Marlborough parish, and Preshute White Horse is carved into
Granham Hill to the west of the A345, just over the northern Savernake boundary.
The forest is close to Marlborough's southern boundary, and the hospital at Forest Hill is within
Savernake parish, before the A4 out of Marlborough enters Mildenhall parish, also represented by Marlborough.
The northern area of  Little Bedwyn parish is immediately east, before the A4 leaves for West Berkshire at  Froxfield.
The Warren is a hamlet in the north of Burbage parish, which along with St Katharine's in the north of  Great Bedwyn
are most often associated with a Savernake postal address, so their websites may be listed here.

1065191.title: Seend
1065191.description:
Seend is a village on the A361 east of  Semington, leading to  Devizes further east.
Seend parish includes the village of Seend Cleeve extending south west along the hamlets of
The Stocks to Seend Head at the western boundary.
The western boundary north includes a bridleway swing-bridge over the Kennet and Avon Canal,
and the northern boundary encloses the canal.
The parish stretches north to include the course of an old railway which ran south of Bowerhill in 
Melksham Without parish, to the west, from Sells Green, north of the canal in the east of the parish.
East of Sells Green,  Rowde parish is north of the canal, then south of the canal at the
hamlet of Martinslade, the eastern boundary is with Poulshot before  Potterne.
This category represents the parish of Bulkington to the south of Seend, whereas websites for
Keevil to the south west are included with those for  Steeple Ashton.

North of the A338,  Little Bedwyn is the next parish on the county boundary, 
Great Bedwyn is to the north west, Marten to the east is in  Little Bedwyn parish.
Shalbourne parish has small settlements including Bagshot and Stype to the north, and Rivar and Oxenwood to the south.

1059540.title: Somerford
1059540.description:
This category lists websites for both Great and Little Somerford, Wiltshire parishes respectively
south and north of the River Avon, south east of  Malmesbury, and north of the M4 motorway.
Great Somerford village is on the south bank of the River Avon, served on by minor roads.
The Avon is the eastern parish boundary, where it is bridged to  Daunstey, by a minor road
giving access to  Lyneham further south east.
Another minor road leads south to Lower Seagry, then Upper Seagry, in the parish of  Seagry.
North of Upper Seagry, the hamlet of Startley is in Great Somerford parish, before the land drops
to Gabriel's Well and the hamlet of Rodbourne Bottom, where two minor roads are bridged
by the railway, in to the village of Rodbourne, in  Corston parish to the north west.
The northern parish boundary with Little Somerford meanders with the River Avon, which is
bridged by a minor road directly north of Great Somerford village.
The road leads under the railway, before Little Somerford village.
North of this village, the B4042 takes road traffic from Malmesmbury at Burton Hill, to  Brinkworth.
Lea and Cleverton are directly north of the B4042.

510796.description:

hamlets of Little Wishford at the north, and Chilhampton at the south of the parish.
This category also represents Great Wishford, a village across Stoford Bridge, and parish along the west bank
of the River Wylye, south of Stapleford parish represented by the  Steeple Langford category.
The eastern boundary of South Newton parish is along the A360 road, with Woodford parish,
represented by the  Woodford Valley category.

The B3109 leads north to  Box and  Corsham,  Atworth is to the east, and  Holt is to the outh east.

Southwick is the Wiltshire parish on the boundary with Somerset, south west of  Trowbridge on the A361 road to  Beckington.

Southwick Country Park separates the conurbation of Southwick from Trowbridge, then to the east,
North Bradley is the parish north of Heywood, represented by  Westbury to the south east.
The village of Yarnbrook at the junction, where the A363 meets the A360, is within
North Bradley parish, and websites for North Bradley are listed here.

South of Stapleford the A36 heads south through  South Newton parish, north of  Wilton.
Hanging Langford connected by a minor road south of the Nadder, is within Steeple Langford parish,
along with Little Langford to its east, and the parish extends south, up the downs,
where the remains of Grim's Ditch form the southern boundary with  Dinton parish.

The parish also includes two railway bridges over the Nadder.

1062320.title: Tidworth
1062320.description:
Tidworth is a town on the A3026 south west of  Ludgershal­l.
Perham Down is a village within Tidworth parish, separating the town from the Hampshire border,
providing a route to  Andover.
Swinton Barracks dominate this village, whereas Tidworth is traditionally an army garrison town, where
Tidworth Camp dominates, with Salisbury Plain providing their traing area to the west.
The A338 leads north to  Collingbourne Ducis, and south through Shipton Bellinger
to join the A303 before  Cholderton.

510715.title: Trowbridge
510715.description:
Trowbridge is the county town of Wiltshire, based on it historical role from Roman times, on the River Biss,
through to the industrial revolution, when the Kennet and Avon Canal was bringing coal from Somerset,
to supply steam-powered manufacturing of clothing and blankets in mills sourced by the county's wool.
For a county town it is relatively close to  Bath, separated from the Somerset boundary only
by  Westwood, Wingfield and  Southwick.
Development has extended into North Bradley, directly south, before Heywood parish
on the A350, represented by  Westbury further south.
At Yarnbrook the A350 turns north to avoid Trowbridge, passing north through West Ashton parish,
before Great Hinton, separated from the east of Trowbridge by  Hilperton.
Staverton is directly north east, where the Kennet and Avon Canal leaves Trowbridge parish
forming the boundary between Hilperton and Staverton, on the way eastwards to  Devizes.
North of Trowbridge, the A363 leads to  Bradford-on-Avon.

The River Dun flows into West Dean parish, formerly feeding the remains of Salisbury and Southampton Canal,

South of Westbury, the A350 leads to  Warminster via  Upton Scudamore.
The southern boundary of Westbury parish, with Upton Scudamore encloses Chalford and Westbury Leigh
which have become suburbs of Westbury.
The parish of Dilton Marsh separates Westbury from the county boundary with  Somerset's Mendips,

The northern boundary, known as Avoncliff, features an aqueduct where the Kennet and Avon Canal

The southern boundary is with the Wiltshire parish of Wingfield, which has a small village, served by the

507837.title: Government
507837.description:
This category tree is for websites relating to all aspects of government in The United Kingdom.
The UK has three levels of Government - central, regional and local.
Central:
Each of the four countries of the UK are represented in the House of Commons,
by Members of Parliament.
Regional:
Three of these countries have devolved powers;  Northern Ireland Assembly,
The Scottish Parliament  and  National Assembly for Wales.
England is not devolved from the UK Parliament, but the population of London first warranted
regional division in a London Assembly administered by the Mayor of London
Subsequently other areas of England opted for a mayor as described in  England: Regions.
Statutory bodies working with UK Ministries and various research organisations,
may also have websites listed in sub-categories here.
Local:
Local government websites tend to be duplicated across Curlie.
  1. Once at the most appropriate  Locality for the scope of their administration,
  2. Together as a UK Topic, according to  County, Unitary Authority, District Council and Town Council.
For details please see  UK: Government: Communities and Local Government
 
For sites which relate to the discussions on the European Union,
please suggest sites to  UK: Society and Culture: Issues: European Union: Opinion
From there, enough websites may accumulate to justify a topic's own category such as:
For UK websites about the discussions on leaving the European Union, see:
UK: Society and Culture: Issues: European Union: Brexit 
For other non-EU issues for which there is no separate category yet:
UK: Society and Culture: Politics: Issues:.
