links.title: Lord Faulkner of Worcester
links.description: Personal site containing a record of the peer's interests and activities since his appointment in 1999.

links.title: Lords of the Blog
links.description: A collaborative blog written by Members of the House of Lords for the purposes of public engagement.

links.title: Kirkhope, Timothy
links.description: Former Conservative Member of the European Parliament for the Yorkshire and the Humber, elevated to Lord Kirkhope of Harrogate. Provides press releases, a biography, contact details, and social media.

links.title: Gillan, Cheryl
links.description: Former Conservative MP for Chesham and Amersham.

links.title: Altmann, Dr. Ros
links.description: Official personal information on Baroness Altmannl CBE, who was Minister of State for Pensions between May 2015 and July 2016. Includes biography, career as an investment banker, economist and pensions industry adviser.

links.title: Beith, Alan
links.description: Article updated by the public on the former Liberal Democrat MP for Berwick-upon-Tweed, elevated to the Lords in 2015. Includes biography, with references and related links.

1060824.title: Evans, Baroness of Bowes Park
1060824.description: Member of the House of Lords Lord Temporal  Life Peerage since September 2014  Leader of the House of Lords  Lord Keeper of the Privy Seal since July 2016  Full member of the Cabinet as Leader of the House of Lords since 2016

links.title: Wikipedia: Natalie Evans, Baroness Evans of Bowes Park
UK Parliament: Baroness Evans of Bowes Park
links.description: Parliamentary career, contributions, experience, voting record and contact information.

links.title: Gov UK: The Rt Hon Baroness Evans of Bowes Park
links.description: Brief biography and roles in the House of Lords and governemnt appointed the Conservative Cabinet in 2016.

507966.title: Postal Services
507966.description: Official websites of public sector postal service organisations.

links.title: Post Office
links.description: Full details of the services available, including banking, foreign exchange, licences of all kinds and passports. Local post-office finder.

links.title: Royal Mail Group
links.description: Umbrella group for Royal Mail, Post Office and Parcel Force. Includes 'about us' section, with details of community initiatives and recruitment.

links.title: Royal Mail
links.description: Corporate information, online sales of stamps and envelopes, tools including post-code finder and postal rates calculator. Also advice on direct marketing and stamp collecting.

links.title: The Postal Museum
links.description: Visitor information, details of collections and exhibitions, online catalogue, and educational resources. Located in Camden.

links.title: UK Package Postal Calculator
links.description: Search and view current postage rates for Royal Mail services. Returns various services on one page, aimed at users of online auction sites.

links.title: Royal Mail Technical
links.description: Gives various forms of technical assistance to users of Mailsort, Presstream and Walksort.

links.title: Guardian Unlimited Special Reports - Postal Service
links.description: News and analysis continuing coverage includes official documents and related links.

507846.title: Reform
507846.description: Websites of organisations (governmental and otherwise) promoting the reform of government in the UK.

links.title: Committee on Standards in Public Life
links.description: AKA the Wicks Committee. Responsible for regulating the conduct of public officials.

507993.title: Regulatory Bodies
507993.description: Official websites of UK Government regulatory bodies.

links.title: Charity Commission for England and Wales
links.description: Regulates the administration and affairs of registered UK charities. Provides a searchable database of registered UK charities and advice and policies on charitable activities.

links.title: Information Commissioner
links.description: Enforces data protection and freedom of information legislation. Includes searchable Data Protection Register.

links.title: HM Courts & Tribunals Service
links.description: Official information about most of the UK courts and tribunals, their responsibilities and how to use them.

links.title: Gov.UK: Departments, Agencies and Public Bodies
links.description: Resource for links to Ministeries, non-ministerial departments, organisations and high profile groups, including devolved administrations.

links.title: Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman
links.description: Information on how to complain about improper or unfair acts or poor service from UK central government bodies and the NHS in England.

508003.title: Broadcasting and Leisure
508003.description: Official websites of UK Government regulatory bodies responsible for broadcasting and leisure matters.

links.title: Advertising Standards Authority
links.description: ASA. Regulates the advertising industry.

links.title: Office of Communications (Ofcom)
links.description: Independent regulator and competition authority for the UK communications industries, with responsibilities across television, radio, telecommunications and wireless communications services. Includes sections on codes and guidelines, consultations, consumer guides, research and contact information.

links.title: Gambling Commission
links.description: Regulatory body for casinos, bingo clubs, gaming machines and the larger society and all local authority lotteries in Great Britain.

508002.title: Employment and Education
508002.description: Official websites of UK Government regulatory bodies responsible for employment and education matters.

links.title: Office for Standards in Education
links.description: OFSTED. Regulates standards of teaching in schools and colleges.

links.title: Pensions Ombudsman
links.description: Resolves disputes about the way that pension schemes are run. Includes information about the services and powers of the Ombudsman, with details of how to make a complaint.

links.title: The Pensions Regulator
links.description: Regulates work-based pensions arrangements. Information and guidance for employers, staff and trustees.

links.title: Central Arbitration Committee
links.description: Independent body adjudicating on applications relating to the recognition and derecognition of trade unions. Decisions, and press notices.

links.title: Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education (OIA)
links.description: Independent student complaints scheme under the Higher Education Act 2004. Information on how to complain, list of participating institutions, corporate documents.

links.title: Commission for Equality and Human Rights
links.description: New all-embracing body for equality and human rights in the UK. Replaces CRE, DRC and EOC in October 2007.

links.title: Office of the Schools Adjudicator
links.description: Information on how adjudicators deal with disputés about school admission policies.

508005.title: Finance and Auditing
508005.description: Official websites of UK Government regulatory bodies responsible for finance and auditing matters.

links.title: Financial Ombudsman
links.description: Provides assistance in resolving complaints against bank, building society, financial adviser, insurance company, investment firm, stockbroker or unit trust company.

links.title: Government Actuary's Department
links.description: Provides actuarial advice, mainly to public sector clients. Includes corporate information, publications and job advertisements.

links.title: Bona Vacantia
links.description: Responsible for administering the estates of persons who die intestate without known kin and collecting the assets of dissolved companies and failed trusts. Provides assistance for companies and estates.

links.title: National Audit Office
links.description: The NAO audits most public-sector bodies in the UK and produces value for money reports into the implementation of Government policies. Recent reports, press releases, and information about current studies.

links.title: Financial Reporting Council
links.description: The parent of the Accounting Standards Board and the Financial Reporting Review Panel, the three together promoting good financial reporting.

links.title: The Panel on Takeovers and Mergers
links.description: Administers the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers, and supervises takeovers, ensuring fair treatment for all shareholders.

links.title: Office of the Public Guardian
links.description: Controls money and property on behalf of people who are not mentally capable of doing so themselves. Provides forms and background information.

links.title: Upper Tribunal (Tax and Chancery)
links.description: Information about tribunals which hear appeals against HMRC decisions.

508006.title: Health and Housing
508006.description: Official websites of UK Government regulatory bodies responsible for health and housing matters.

links.title: Human Fertilization and Embryology Commission (HFEC)
links.description: Licences and regulates fertility treatment and research.

links.title: Health and Safety Executive (HSE)
links.description: Protects against risks to health or safety arising out of work activities, conducts and sponsors research, promotes training, provides information and advice, and proposes regulations and codes of practice.

links.title: National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence
links.description: Independent Government body providing national guidance on the promotion of good health and the prevention and treatment of ill health.

links.title: Food Standards Agency
links.description: Provides information on food safety in the UK, including news, regulations and research.

links.title: Scottish Medicines Consortium
links.description: Advises NHS bodies in Scotland about the status of new medicines.  Advice, submissions, minutes.

links.title: Housing and Housing Policy
links.description: Information from the Department for Communities and Local Government concerning policy and information on housing issues.

links.title: General Medical Council (GMC)
links.description: Regulates the activities of practising medical doctors. Includes guidance for doctors and the public.

508004.title: Industry and Commerce
508004.description: Official websites of UK Government regulatory bodies responsible for industry and commerce issues.

links.title: Competition Appeal Tribunal
links.description: The CAT hears appeals against competition law decisions of the OFT, sector regulators and the Competition Commission. Transcripts and judgements for all cases.

links.title: The Coal Authority
links.description: Regulates the licensing of coalmines and residual functions of the former British Coal.

links.title: Competition and Markets Authority
links.description: Responsible for investigating allegations of restrictive practices and monopolies.

links.title: Regulator of Community Interest Companies
links.description: Registers Community Interest Companies and enforces the statutory asset lock. Information, guidance and a list of CICs.

links.title: Gangmasters Licensing Authority
links.description: Aims to curb the exploitation of workers in the agriculture, horticulture, shellfish gathering and associated processing and packaging industries. Provides information for labour providers, users, and workers.

links.title: Security Industry Authority
links.description: Manages the licensing of the private security industry as set out in the Private Security Industry Act 2001. Includes legislation and information on how to get or renew a licence.

507994.title: Utilities and Transport
507994.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for utilities and transportation issues.

507999.title: Aviation
507999.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for aviation.

links.title: Civil Aviation Authority
links.description: CAA. Regulates the financial affairs and safety responsibilities of UK airlines and airports. Includes a variety of consultation and policy documents.

links.title: Air Accidents Investigation Branch
links.description: Responsible for the investigation of civil aircraft accidents and serious incidents within the UK. Provides background on the AAIB, regulatory information and bulletins on accidents and serious incidents.

507998.title: Buses and Coaches
507998.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for bus and coach services.

links.title: Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency
links.description: Oversees MoT testing, supports the traffic commissioners and enforces standards of maintenance for road vehicles. Corporate information only.

links.title: Traffic Commissioners
links.description: Page on Department for Transport website about the Traffic Commissioners who licence lorry, bus and coach operators. Very little information.

507997.title: Electricity and Gas
507997.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for electricity and/or gas supply.

links.title: ELEXON
links.description: Balancing and settlement code company, manages the electricity and trading arrangements of England and Wales. Details of panel, signatories, papers and other information.

links.title: Office of Gas and Electricity Markets
links.description: Ofgem. Regulates the electricity and gas markets in Great Britain.  All consultation and decision documents, and many consultation responses from regulated companies and other organisations.

links.title: Health and Safety Executive - Downstream gas
links.description: The HSE oversee safety regulation in downstream gas.  Includes codes of practice, incident reports, and information for the industry.

links.title: Office for Nuclear Regulation
links.description: UK Government agency for the safety regulation of the civilian nuclear industry. Provides policy documents and reports on incidents.

links.title: Health and Safety Executive - Offshore oil and gas
links.description: HSE pages relating to the regulation of safety cases for offshore gas platforms.

links.title: Joint Office of Gas Transporters
links.description: Responsible for the governance of gas industry-wide arrangements and codes, particularly the Uniform Network Code.  Full code text available (PDF).

links.title: Utility Regulator
links.description: Regulates electricity, gas, water and wastewater services in Northern Ireland. Consultations and decision documents.

508000.title: Postal Services
508000.description: UK regulatory bodies for postal services.

links.title: Ofcom
links.description: Information from the regulator of the postal market in the UK. Includes policy and consultation documents.

507996.title: Railways
507996.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for railways.

links.title: Office of Rail and Road
links.description: Independent safety and economic regulator for the railway industry in Great Britain. Consultation and decision papers, speeches and a public register.

links.title: Victimised Whistleblowers - A Trade Union Perspective
links.description: Offers an account of safety campaigning from a workers' representative viewpoint.

links.title: Transport Focus
links.description: Independent public body set up by the Government to protect the interests of Britain's rail passengers. Provides details about the body and its work, together with advice and information for passengers.

links.title: Rail Accident Investigation Branch
links.description: The RAIB (administratively part of the DfT) is the independent railway accident investigation organisation for the UK. Investigation reports, information leaflets, consultation documents.

508001.title: Telecommunications
508001.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for telecommunications services.

links.title: Office of Communications (Ofcom)
links.description: Independent regulator and competition authority for the UK communications industries, with responsibilities across television, radio, telecommunications and wireless communications services. Includes sections on codes and guidelines, consultations, consumer guides, research and contact information.

507995.title: Water and Sewerage
507995.description: Official websites of UK regulatory bodies responsible for water and sewerage services.

links.title: Office of Water Services (Ofwat)
links.description: Regulates water and sewerage providers in England and Wales.  Consultation documents, speeches, regulatory determinations, and information about the industry's performance.

links.title: Environment Agency
links.description: The EA regulates water abstraction and effluent disposal by water companies and others.

links.title: Scottish Environment Protection Agency (SEPA)
links.description: Regulatory agency for waste, water, land and air in Scotland. Provides information on environmental regulations, guidance, publications and education.

links.title: Water Industry Commission for Scotland (WICS)
links.description: Regulates Scottish Water, the State-owned company providing water and sewerage services in Scotland. Consultation and decision documents.

links.title: Consumer Council for Water (CCWater)
links.description: Represents consumers of water and sewerage services in England and Wales. Press notices, some leaflets and other publications.

links.title: Drinking Water Quality Regulator for Scotland (DWQR)
links.description: Regulates drinking water quality in Scotland. Access to reports and information about the regulator's role.

links.title: Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI)
links.description: Regulates drinking water quality in England and Wales. Industry and consumer information.

links.title: Northern Ireland Environment Agency
links.description: Executive agency for the protection and conservation of the natural and built environment in Northern Ireland. Includes the Drinking Water Inspectorate (NI).

links.title: UK Research and Innovation
links.description: The UK Research Councils are established under Royal Charter to fund research in the UK via grants, fellowships, laboratories and central facilities. Site provides information about the Research Councils and their activities.

links.title: UKRI: Arts and Humanities Research Council
links.description: Provides funding and support to UK researchers in three programmes: advanced research; postgraduate research and training; and special funding for museums, libraries and galleries.

507864.title: BBSRC
507864.description: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council

links.title: UKRI: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council
links.description: BBSRC is a funding agency for academic research and training in the biosciences at universities and institutes throughout the UK. The research they fund aims to improve the understanding of living organisms and biological systems.

links.title: John Innes Centre (JIC)
links.description: JIC undertakes research aimed at understanding the genome organisation and function of plants and some key microbes, the genetic and cellular basis of growth and development, key molecular pathways and valuable products and the molecular basis of plant disease and its control.

links.title: The Babraham Institute
links.description: The Babraham Institute carries out research and advanced training with relevance to the biomedical, biotechnological, pharmaceutical and healthcare research and user communities.

links.title: Silsoe Research Institute ( SRI )
links.description: SRI provides expertise in the engineering and physical sciences and mathematics to support the agri-food industries.

links.title: Quadram Institute Bioscience
links.description: Specialist in food research focused on health, undertakiung independent basic and strategic research. Profile, targets, case studies, Clinical Research Facility at the Colnet Campus of the University of East Anglia.

links.title: Roslin Institute
links.description: The Roslin Institute concentrates on UK farm animal science research, combining the advances in molecular and cellular biology to develop new scientific opportunities in biotechnology, animal production, breeding and welfare.

links.title: The Pirbright Institute
links.description: A world centre for research and training in fundamental, strategic and applied research on infectious diseases of farm animals.

507861.title: EPSRC
507861.description: The Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) funds high quality research and postgraduate training in engineering and the physical sciences, predominantly in UK universities.

links.title: UKRI: Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council
links.description: EPSRC funds research and postgraduate training in engineering and the physical sciences at universities and other organisations throughout the UK.

507868.title: ESRC
507868.description: The Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) is the UK's leading research and training agency addressing economic and social concerns.

links.title: UKRI: Economic and Social Research Council
links.description: The Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) is the UK's leading research and training agency addressing economic and social concerns.

507860.title: MRC
507860.description: The Medical Research Council (MRC) encourages and supports high-quality research with the aim of maintaining and improving human health

links.title: UKRI: Medical Research Council
links.description: MRC encourages and supports research with the aim of maintaining and improving human health

507862.title: NERC
507862.description: The Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) funds and carries out impartial environmental science research.

links.title: The Natural Environment Research Council
links.description: The Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) funds and carries out impartial environmental science research

links.title: British Geological Survey
links.description: The BGS is one of the centres that makes up the Natural Environment Research Council. It is active in areas such as land-use planning, waste disposal, hydrocarbons exploration, civil engineering, minerals extraction, contaminated land, seismic and geohazard evaluation and understanding climate change.

links.title: British Antarctic Survey
links.description: BAS is responsible for almost all of the British Government's scientific research in the Antarctic, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands. Describes the work of BAS and includes information on subjects including conservation and climate change.

507866.title: STFC
507866.description: The Science and Technology Facilities Council was formed in 2007 by a merger of the former Particle Physics and Astronomy Research Council (PPARC) and the Central Laboratory of the Research Councils (CCLRC). The new entity directs and co-ordinates the funding of research in national and international programmes in particle physics, technology, astronomy, cosmology and space science.

links.title: UKRI: Science and Technology Facilities Council
links.description: One of Europe's largest multidisciplinary research organisations supporting scientists and engineers world-wide. Details of facilities, support and grants.

507867.title: Scientific Sites
507867.description: Scientific sites for the UK Particle Physics and Astronomy Research Council

links.title: Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes (ING)
links.description: The Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes (ING) operates the 4.2m William Herschel Telescope, the 2.5m Isaac Newton Telescope and the 1.0m Jacobus Kapteyn Telescope on behalf of the Particle Physics and Astronomy Research Council (PPARC) of the United Kingdom and the Netherlands Organization for Scientific Research (NWO) of the Netherlands. The ING is located at the Roque de Los Muchachos Observatory, La Palma, Spain.

links.title: UK Astronomy Technology Centre (ATC)
links.description: The ATC, based at the Royal Observatory Edinburgh, aims to be the UK's National Centre for the design and production of state of the art astronomical technology

links.title: Central Laser Facility
links.description: The Central Laser Facility (CLF) at RAL operates several high power lasers; Astra, Vulcan and the Lasers for Science Facility (LSF). These serve the university community in plasma physics, biological and chemical fields.

507949.title: Rural Affairs
507949.description: Official Central Government sites concerning Rural Affairs in the United Kingdom.

links.title: MAGIC
links.description: Multi-Agency Geographic Information for the Countryside brings together definitive rural designation boundaries and information about rural land-based schemes.

links.title: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA)
links.description: The UK Government department tasked with issues such as the environment, rural development, the countryside, wildlife, animal welfare and sustainable development.  Formerly MAFF, the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Foods.

507838.title: Science and Technology
507838.description: Official websites of UK governmental, regulatory and advisory bodies responsible for science and technology issues in the United Kingdom.

links.title: UK Space Agency
links.description: Britain's space agency which advises and acts on behalf of Government and the Research Councils, to provide a focus for UK civil space policies.

links.title: The UK Meteorological Office
links.description: Includes latest weather, research and information on the history of the organisation.

links.title: Foresight Projects
links.description: Strategic planning programme which brings people, knowledge and ideas together to look ahead and prepare for future technological and environmental challenges.

links.title: Council for Science and Technology
links.description: Government advisory body on major science and technology issues of strategic importance to the United Kingdom. Site provides information about the CST's membership, activities and reports.

507857.title: Trade and Industry
507857.description: Official websites of UK governmental, regulatory and advisory bodies responsible for trade and industry matters in the United Kingdom.

links.title: Companies House
links.description: Responsible for the registration and provision of UK company information. This site describes the range of activities and the statutory obligations of limited liability companies.

links.title: Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service
links.description: ACAS is an organisation devoted to preventing and resolving employment disputes. This site provides information on how to contact ACAS as well as on-line information for employers and employees on a range of issues including effective communications.

links.title: Export Credits Guarantee Department
links.description: The ECGD is the government department responsible for providing financial and insurance assistance to exporters of UK capital goods and services. The site describes their products, services, information on credit lines and includes a FAQ.

links.title: Competition and Markets Authority
links.description: Includes a list of reports dating back to the 1950s with summaries of some of the most recent reports.

links.title: Business Link
links.description: Self-help portal of action-focused information for small and medium businesses, linking to all relevant ministries and departments.

links.title: UK Trade and Investment
links.description: Site providing information and assistance to UK industry on exporting and export policy.

links.title: The UK Intellectual Property Office
links.description: Information about Intellectual Property especially Copyright, Designs, Patents and Trade Marks.

links.title: The Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS)
links.description: Offers information on a range of services provided by the Department to help businesses.

links.title: Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy
links.description: The Department for Energy and Climate Change's Oil and Gas Directorate deals with licensing and regulation issues, market promotion and the distribution of information regarding the UK's oil and gas reserves.

links.title: Insolvency Service
links.description: Provides the mechanisms and means for dealing with individual and corporate financial failure and the investigation of fraud and misconduct in insolvencies. Site contains guidance material and downloadable forms.

links.title: National Measurement and Regulation Office
links.description: The role of the executive agency in type approval, EMC and environmental testing, such as ensuring that micropipette measurement is accurate, fair and legal, for the Department of Trade and Industry.

links.title: Tracker
links.description: Offers UK public sector and government contract information, also providing tender information throughout the UK and Europe.

links.title: The Queen's Awards for Enterprise
links.description: A Queen's Award is the highest honour that can be bestowed on a UK company. This site explains about the awards system, how to qualify, the review system and lists the award winners.

links.title: Citizens Advice
links.description: Provides information and links to sources of further advice on issues of concern to general consumers, according to laws in Northern Ireland, Scotland, England and Wales.

links.title: Uktradeinfo
links.description: Customs and Excise offering accurate and up to date trade information for exports and imports.

links.title: Great Britain-China Centre
links.description: An executive non-departmental public body of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office established to support UK-China relations.

507970.title: Transport
507970.description: Official websites of UK governmental, regulatory and advisory bodies responsible for transportation and planning issues in the United Kingdom.

links.title: Urban Transport Group
links.description: Network that promotes urban transport issues. Policy documents, consultation responses, research papers.

links.title: Transport Scotland
links.description: Responsible for the delivery of major infrastructure projects and for overseeing the operation of the Scottish transport networks. Information about schemes, reports, news.

links.title: Act TravelWise
links.description: Association of local authorities and other organisations to promote sustainable transport. Includes campaign news, advice for schools and businesses, and free downloadable materials.

links.title: Transport Analysis Guidance
links.description: Guidance on the conduct of transport analysis studies: multi-modal methods (GOMMMS), safety and environment, and use of models. Run by DfT.

links.title: Commission for Integrated Transport
links.description: CfIT. Established to provide independent advice to the Government on the implementation of integrated transport policy and to monitor developments in transport and the environment. Provides information on the role and membership of the Commission, plus copies of its reports and publications. [Archive]

links.title: The Chartered Institution of Highways & Transportation (CIHT)
links.description: Aims to provide a forum for the exchange of technical information and views on highways and transport policy; to make roads safer for the travelling public; and to encourage training and development to meet today's requirements.

links.title: UK Transport Statistics Information
links.description: Official reports, publications and data on transport usage within the UK.

links.title: Department for Transport
links.description: Responsible for transport issues (except when devolved), in particular railway franchising and a range of executive agencies. Policy papers, and speeches.

links.title: Disabled Persons Transport Advisory Committee
links.description: Responsible for advising the UK Government on access for disabled people to transport and the built environment. Provides information on access to various modes of transport and details of the Committee's work.

links.title: DfT OLR Holdings Limited
links.description: DOHL maintains the continuity of passenger rail services if a passenger rail franchise terminates and there is no immediate replacement.

507973.title: Maritime
507973.description: Official websites of UK governmental, statutory or regulatory bodies responsible for maritime issues.

links.title: Trinity House Lighthouse Service
links.description: Responsible for operating and maintaining the country's lighthouses.

links.title: Caledonian MacBrayne Ferries
links.description: Hebridean and Clyde ferry services. Company information, route information, and online booking.

links.title: Her Majesty's Nautical Almanac Office
links.description: Produces the Astronomical Almanac, the Nautical Almanac, Astronomical Phenomena, the Star Almanac and the UK Air Almanac.

links.title: Marine Accident Investigation Branch
links.description: Provides information on the work of the MAIB, which is responsible for investigating all types of marine accidents, both to ships and to people on board them.

links.title: UK maritime sector policies
links.description: Information from the UK Department for Transport on maritime regulation and safety matters.

links.title: Maritime and Coastguard Agency
links.description: Information on maritime matters, Merchant Shipping Notices, Marine Guidance Notes and Marine Information Notes.

507971.title: Railways
507971.description: Official websites of UK governmental, statutory or regulatory bodies responsible for railway-related issues.

links.title: British Transport Police
links.description: National police service for the railways in Great Britain. Provides information on regional contacts and BTP policy on policing sporting events.

links.title: Rail Accident Investigation Branch
links.description: Independent railway accident investigation organisation for the UK. Details of procedures and regulations, news, and publications.

links.title: Crossrail International
links.description: Specialist advisory practice, wholly owned by the UK government’s Department for Transport (DfT), that provides strategic advice globally to client organisations developing and delivering complex rail schemes.

507972.title: Roads
507972.description: Official websites of UK governmental, statutory or regulatory bodies responsible for roads-related issues.

links.title: Traffic Penalty Tribunal
links.description: Independent tribunal that considers appeals by motorists whose vehicles have been issued with a parking ticket in England and Wales.

links.title: Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency
links.description: Ensure that goods vehicles, buses, coaches, cars and motorbikes are maintained to minimum legal standards.

links.title: Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency
links.description: DVLA. Registers drivers and vehicles and collects vehicle taxation.

links.title: Vehicle Certification Agency
links.description: Describes the VCA's role as the UK's national approval authority for new road vehicles.

links.title: THINK! Road Safety
links.description: Information and resources on road safety.

links.title: Driving Standards Agency
links.description: Includes details on good driving practice and the current driving test regulations.

links.title: Manual for Streets
links.description: Joint project by the Department for Transport and the Department for Communities and Local Government, to develop guidance to a range of practitioners on effective street design. News, project information, and current drafts.

507845.title: Welfare
507845.description: Official UK Governmental sites relating to welfare and social security matters.

links.title: Gov.UK: Child Maintenance
links.description: Government information about financial support towards childrens' living costs parents have separated. Details of eligibility, application, non-payment, disagreements, complaints, appeals and other contacts for the UK Child Support Agency.

links.title: Gov.UK: State Pension
links.description: Provides information and resources on retirement pensions for individuals, employers and providers.

links.title: Gov.UK: Veterans
links.description: Offering help from the Ministry of Defence for ex-service personnel and dependents, on issues including benefits, housing and welfare. Includes policy relating war pensions and the armed forces covenant, and claim forms.

links.title: The Pensions Regulator
links.description: Statutory regulator for occupational pension schemes in the UK. Provides information for business advisers, trustees individuals and employers, including public service, with document library of publications, links to videos and social media, and contacts.

links.title: Gov.UK Policy Paper 2010 to 2015: Housing for Older and Vulnerable People
links.description: Information published by the coalition government on their approach to the problem of homelessness and rough sleeping.

links.title: Gov.UK: Statistics at DWP
links.description: Provides published and upcoming analysis, for families, health, employment support schemes, unemployment, housing, and living standards. Includes policies and procedures, access, and contacts.

links.title: Gov.UK: Workplace and Personal Pensions
links.description: Official information for the over 50s, voluntary retirement, and planning income in old age, with links to related topics.

links.title: Department for Work and Pensions
links.description: Government department responsible for welfare and employment issues.  Formerly the Department of Social Security (DSS) and Department for Education and Employment (DfEE).

534519.title: McTimoney
534519.description:
This category lists websites specifically about the branch of Chiropractice originating in Banbury in 1951, named after
John McTimoney, who developed the chiropractic technique as a non-invasive holistic treatment of disease.
He used the sense of touch in the fingers of both hands, to analyse a patient’s entire skeleton in order to detect misalignments.
Treatment to achieve realignment of the vertebrae, often using his toggle recoil thrust produced immediate comfort of the patient.

534316.title: ADD and ADHD
534316.description:
A spectrum of neurological disorders, increasingly recognised as affecting children, young people and adults, and manifesting themselves (very simplistically) as
  • overactive behaviour/hyperactivity
  • impulsive behaviour
  • difficulty in paying attention
These may cause difficulties within families and in school.

ADD refers to problems in concentration and attention; ADHD refers to ADD plus overactive and impulsive behaviours. The "official" UK term, Hyperkinetic Disorders, covers the aspects of hyperactivity and impulsive behaviours.

The causes of ADD/ADHD appear (currently) to be a mixture of genetic and environmental factors (possibly including diet). Children who have suffered brain injury or illness may also exhibit similar symptomatic behaviours.

534312.title: Autism Spectrum
534312.description: Autism is a lifelong condition that was first identified as a new syndrome in 1943. Early theories of its cause and diagnostic systems focused on an emotional abnormality. Evidence now suggests that autism is due to physical dysfunction within the brain, which leads to a difference in development, not just a delay. Key features that characterise autism have been identified as the ‘triad of impairments’. These affect social interaction, social communication and imagination. The manifestations of each impairment vary according to the general level of cognitive ability and the existence of any additional problems. This results in a continuum of need, or a range of conditions called the ‘autistic spectrum disorders’.

534305.title: Self Injury
534305.description:
This category is for sites emanating from and relating to the United Kingdom, in English, on the topic of Self Injury. Nations included are England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales. Self Injury can go by many names, such as:
  • Cutting
  • Self Injurious Behavior
  • Deliberate Self Harm
  • Self Inflicted Violence
  • Repetitive Self-Harm Syndrome
The UK has one of the highest rates of self-injury in Europe. Self Injury is far more widespread than is generally realised, especially in adolescents under stress. It also seems to be more common among women, partly because men are more likely to express strong feelings, such as anger, outwardly. However, people from all walks of life self-injure and, unfortunately, the true extent of the disorder is unknown. Research shows that where it is acceptable to talk about, many women, as well as some men, reveal that they have self-injured at some time. Diana, Princess of Wales, in an interview on the BBC in 1995, gave the disorder a face for the general public. Sites included in this category, and its sub-categories, are potentially triggering.

1063014.title: Covid
1063014.description:
This category leads to websites about the effects of the Coronavirus SARS-Cov-2 in the UK.
This includes the first recognised cases in the UK of the respiratory disease assigned the name Covid-19, first originating
in Wuhan China in December 2019, subsequent sequencing of its constituent RNA, and attempts to stop its spread.
Websites for the global pandemic aspects of the disease should be listed in the top  Health . . Covid-19 category,
where it is regarded as a Respiratory Disorder.
This category includes websites about the non-respiratory symptoms named Long Covid, the various mutations recognised
in RNA sequence, the methods proposed to reduce its spread, cure symptoms and infectivity, particularly in the UK.
Websites purely about the status of immunisation against SARS-Cov-2 type coronaviruses should be listed in the Vaccines category.

1063240.title: Vaccines
1063240.description:
This category leads to websites about the Vaccines against Coronavirus SARS-Cov-2 proposed for the UK market,
subject their approval by the Government's regulatory authority, MHRA.
For those not expected to have requests or approval, follow links in the top  Health: Covid-19 category.
In 2020, there were two novel approaches, taken by more than one research team and manufacturing partner.
Websites referring to just one of these may be listed in the appropriate subcategory.
This category only includes therapies intended to induce long term immunological resistance,
though this may include those directed against the various mutations recognised in RNA sequence.
Until there are sufficient websites about short-term therapies, such as plasma from ex-patients, monoclonal
antibodies and steriods, or those specifically to relieve the symptoms of Long Covid,
those websites should be listed in the parent category.

1063242.title: Spike Protein
1063242.description:
This category leads to websites about the Vaccines against Coronavirus SARS-Cov-2 proposed for the UK market,
that rely on the injection of the spike protein on surface of the virus, usually using a benign adenovirus as
the vector, to stimulate an immunological response.
In 2020, two forms were developed, one at Oxford Sanger Institute, and the other at Imperial College London.
The Oxford Group partnered with Astra Zenica for vaccine manufacture, and were first to reach phase three clincal trials.
The UK had preordered 100 million doses in advance of regulatory appproval.
In the event, the alternative developed by BioNTech, manufactured by Pfizer gained regulatory approval before this.
Websites referring to the use of Covid protein may be listed here.
This category only includes therapies intended to induce long term immunological resistance, though
this may include those directed against the various mutations arising after 2019.

1063241.title: mRNA
1063241.description:
This category leads to websites about the Vaccines against Coronavirus SARS-Cov-2 proposed for the UK market,
that rely on the injection of messenger RNA synthesised to match the sequence of the virus in order
to stimulate an immunological response.
In 2020, there were two manufacturers using this approach, and the UK had preordered that
developed by BioNTech, for manufacture by Pfizer.
Websites referring to this technique may be listed here.

529002.title: Repeaters
529002.description: A repeater takes a received signal and re-transmits it on a different frequency known as the "offset" frequency.   Amateur radio enthusiasts use repeaters to establish contact over a larger distance than would normally be possible, especially when operating mobile from a car or with a low power handheld radio.   Repeaters are positioned on strategic sites chosen for their height, giving a "line of sight" view to the area that they cover and thereby allowing low power devices to communicate through them. For this reason in cities repeaters are often situated on the roof of high-rise buildings, and in rural locations on hilltops.   Amateur repeaters are run out of a dedication to the hobby and not for any commercial gain. They generally use donated equipment and rely on financial donations to cover overheads such as rent.   This category contains sites that are specific to particular repeaters in the United Kingdom and generally will contain details about their construction, operating frequencies and coverage area.

529072.description:
This category serves to guide users to sites for UK Garden Centres and Nurseries that primarily offer help and advice rather than online shopping or directions and a brochure.

Sites are only listed directly in this category if they offer information that is of interest to gardeners across the UK, without attempting to sell their products.  Note that the shopping categories also contain some sites with information about gardening and plants, along with sales.
Nurseries only selling plants are listed under UK.. Shopping .. Gardens: Plants, where as those also selling gardening supplies are included in the UK.. Shopping .. Garden Centres.  Retailers of garden goods without delivering plants, may be found in other parts of UK.. Shopping .. Gardens.

529327.title: Fox
529327.description:
Sites for Hunts in Britain represented by the Masters of Foxhounds Association.
These are packs of hounds that hunt the scent of fox.
Until the 2004 Act has been repealed, instead of being allowed to kill the fox swiftly and naturally, the pack is no longer allowed to take part in the kill.
Some hunts are attempting to maintain their packs by trailhunting the scent of fox.
In countries where there is likely to be attempted prosecution if the hounds change to a live fox, then removal of foxes is offered within the provisions of the Act, to secure the continuation of the sport.
Services such as fox control, collection of fallen stock continue to serve the local community.

The challenge by two members of the Union of Country Sports Workers to overturn the Scottish foxhunting ban by claiming that it infringed human rights failed yesterday when a judge ruled that the legislation was legitimate. The decision will be appealed.

529206.title: Dressage
529206.description:
Dressage has been called an "elegant dance of horse and rider", and has been practiced as an art for centuries.

In the western world the Greeks were among the first to extol this type of equestrian partnership by putting their training methods down in writing. Among the principles espoused was the need to train the horse as a war horse, including all the intricate movements necessary to assist the rider while fighting in close quarters. By necessary, these movements had to be precise and immediate, no matter where the horse was at any particular moment or time, or the soldier risked forfeit of his life. With training, these movements became more rigorously defined, building to a level of detail and precision that often required years of study for both horse and rider to develop and hone.

The ancients may have set the stage for an enduring partnership between the horse and humanity, but it was the French, as great exponents of this art, who were the first to coin it "dressage".

Although the horse no longer participates in the battlefields as it did in the past, the Dressage arts have moved to a higher level in the world of sports, advancing it world-wide on many levels -- from local beginner to international Olympic. It is a beautiful discipline of classic origins -- elegant to watch and a joy to ride.

529423.title: Silat
529423.description: Silat is a general term that comprehensively denotes all Martial Arts based on the originally Southeast Asian (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Southern Philippines) arts of Penca(k) and Silat.   The root philosophy of Penca(k) and Silat in Southeast Asia includes aspects of self defence, social and spiritual ethics, arts, and sports.    Further Martial Arts (i.e. Kun Tao, Pukulan) have contributed to the actual forms of practice worldwide. Besides its native cultures in South East Asia, Penca(k) Silat especially began to flourish in the USA, the Netherlands, and other mainly European countries after World War II.    In South East Asia and other parts of the world a world union of Pencak Silat (PERSILAT, headquarters located in Jakarta, Indonesia) exists, though this organisation is not recognised by all schools. The PERSILAT organises national and worldwide tournaments of Pencak Silat Sports (Olahraga) and Pencak Silat Art Form (Seni Budaya).    According to the description of PERSILAT, one should distinguish between traditional, transitional (semi-modern) and modern type schools. However, this description may not fit completely to describe the forms of Penca(k) Silat schools generally and worldwide.    Though many aspects and terms related to Penca(k) Silat are shared worldwide, a definite use of terminology and its meanings is currently not yet established.

529164.title: Rounders
529164.description: Rounders is a game played between two teams each alternating between batting and fielding. It is a striking and fielding team game, which involves hitting a small, hard, leather-cased ball with a round wooden, plastic or metal bat and then running around four bases in order to score.    The game is regulated by the Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) in the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland and by Rounders England (formerly the National Rounders Association of Great Britain) in England.    Both have different, although similar, game-play and culture. Competitions are held between teams from both traditions with games alternating between codes, often one version being played in the morning and the other in the afternoon.

529176.title: Tchoukball
529176.description: Tchoukball (pronounced Chuke-ball)  is played on an indoor court measuring forty metres by twenty metres (130 feet x 65 feet). At each end there is a 'frame' (a device similar to a trampoline off which the ball bounces) which measures one square metre and a semicircular 'D' measuring three metres (10 feet) out from the frame in all directions. Each team can score on both ends on the field, and comprises twelve players, of which nine may be on the court at any one time. In order to score a point, the ball must be thrown by an attacking player, hit the frame and bounce outside the 'D' without being caught by the defending team. Physical contact is prohibited, and defenders may not attempt to intercept the attacking team's passes. Players may take three steps with the ball, hold the ball for a maximum of three seconds, and teams may not pass the ball more than three times before shooting at the frame.

This category is for websites about miniature railways in the United Kingdom.
These are capable of carrying passengers, though may have only survived as recreational or tourist attractions.
In order qualify as a miniature railway, the separation of the rails must be 20 inches or less.
The website should show this gauge, commonly 15 inch gauge down to 7¼ inch,
but where may also be tracks and locomotives available for 5, 3.5 and 2.5 inch gauge.

529044.title: North Downs Way
529044.description: An inspirational journey. All of the route is available for walkers, some limited sections are suitable for horse riders and cyclists. The trail is easily accessible from neighbouring countries in Europe.    Fact File    Length: 246 km   Start: Farnham, Surrey   Finish: Dover or Canterbury   Terrain: Wide variety of terrain so condition varies along length and in different seasons. Close to villages and towns.   Attractions: Good for day walks and longer distances. Close to London and Continental Europe. The trail is well served by rail and bus services. Various circular walks exist.   This 157 mile (251 km) route traverses some of the finest landscape in South East England and is one of the most accessible and easy to follow long distance routes in the country.    Travellers have long used the scarp of the North Downs as a guide for a safe route across south east England. In prehistoric times the chalk scarp linked with France to form a natural bridge allowing our ancestors to migrate here from other parts of Europe. Pilgrims used the scarp as a marker on their pilgrimage from Canterbury to Winchester for the festival of St. Swithin and then, after the murder of Thomas Beckett at Canterbury, the pilgrimage changed direction from Winchester to Canterbury!   The North Downs Way loosely follows the Pilgrims Way, a 19th century interpretation of where the pilgrims trod, a Victorian National Trail! The North Downs Way passes through two Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty, the Surrey Hills and Kent Downs ? landscapes which have inspired - amongst many others - Vaughn Williams, Charles Dickens, Lewis Carroll and George and Mary Watts.   With excellent rail links to London it is easy to reach the trail. The North Downs Way can either be walked as a whole or in sort sections over a period of time. Whichever way you chose, walk in the footsteps of history, discover the three cathedrals, three palaces, eight castles and a landscape which has inspired many.   - From The Countryside Agency

All the coast path is accessible from the Coastliner bus service. Rail links exist to both ends. Much of the trail is barrier free for equal access making it suitable for people with a disability.    - From The Countryside Agency

529024.description: Horses for courses. Work is currently in progress to develop the route. The southern section, to North Yorkshire will open by 2002 and the rest of the Trail by 2003. Consultation is underway on a proposal for a northern extension, which would ake the route through Cumbria into Northumberland, ending at Byrness in the Kielder Forest Park, just south of the Scottish Border.   Fact File   Length: 330km   Start: Carsington Reservoir or Middleton Top, Derbyshire   Finish: Fat Lamb Inn, Kirkby Stephen, Cumbria  Terrain: No steep gradients, no stiles, mostly on tracks with a mix of surfaces including some grassy sections. Suitable for mountain bikes not touring cycles. Some exposed terrain on the northern section. Horses, riders and cyclists need to be fit to complete the whole route in one journey.  Attractions: 2 National Parks, links to interesting towns and villages including the Settle to Carlisle railway. Bridleway link routes.  - From The Countryside Agency

Attractions: Challenging trail, wild and spectacular scenery. Rail and bus links to start and finish.   - From the Countryside Agency

529020.title: Ridgeway
529020.description: England's oldest road. The whole trail is open to walkers, whilst horse riders and cyclists can enjoy all the western half. Off road vehicles can also use most of the western half, but they are very much in the minority. The Ridgeway Code of Respect should be followed, and is available from the National Trail Office.    Fact File    Length: 137km   Start: Overton Hill near Avebury, Wiltshire   Finish: Ivinghoe Beacon, Buckinghamshire   Terrain: Some parts exposed, broad track sections can become muddy and rutted in winter. Generally easy going walking.   Attractions: Numerous archaelogical sites, good bus and rail links to eastern half.   137 km (85 miles) long, much of it following the ancient chalk ridge route used by prehistoric man, The Ridgeway offers the chance to get away from the bustle of life in this busy part of England. Perfect, but not too strenuous, for long distance use, this Trail is also ideal for day trips or less.  - From The Countryside Agency

529046.title: South Downs Way
529046.description: A precious landscape. This trail is a bridleway along its entire length (designated in 1972 as the first long distance bridleway) and is suitable for cyclists.  Fact File   Length: 161km   Start: Eastbourne, East Sussex   Finish: Winchester, Hampshire  Terrain: Wide grassy tracks, well drained soils, lack of stiles makes it suitable for all ages and abilities.  Attractions: Historic sites and towns and circular routes, rail and bus links to start, finish and places in between.  The 161 kilometre long trail follows the old routes and droveways of ancient man along the chalk escarpment and ridges of the South Downs. The route provides the visitor with the opportunity "to get away from it all" without having to travel too far in this busy part of England. The undulating route provides a wonderful trip for long distance riders as well as walkers. It also provides interesting day trips and short breaks.  - From The Countryside Agency

529040.title: Thames Path
529040.description: A walk along the river.   Fact File   Length: 288km   Start: Near Kemble, Gloucestershire (the source of the River Thames)   Finish: Thames Barrier, Woolwich, London   Terrain: Gentle level walking along the riverbank through farmland, villages, towns and cities. Easy to follow.  Attractions: Good access by bus and train, many historic towns and houses along the way.   The trail follows England's best known river for 294 km / 184 miles as it meanders from its source in Gloucestershire through several rural counties and on into the bustle of the City of London. On its way the Path passes peaceful water meadows rich in wildlife, historic towns and many lovely villages, finishing at the Thames Barrier in Woolwich. Easy to reach by public transport, the Thames Path is accessible for walkers of all ages and abilities. This National Trail can be enjoyed in many ways, whether for an afternoon's stroll, a weekend's break or a full scale, but relatively gentle, trek of its whole length.    - From the Countryside Agency
