1062045.title: Chilterns
1062045.description: This category list websites specifically about The Chiltern Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, for the range of hills spanning north east from the Thames at Goring, Oxfordshire to Dunstaple Downs, Bedfordshire, through the southern part of Buckinghamshire.

links.title: Chilterns AONB
links.description: Official Information for visitors, about wildlife, habitat and conservation projects, on the designated area of outstanding natural beauty, for the range of hills spanning through Bucks, from the Thames at Goring to Dunstaple Downs.

links.title: National Trust: Chilterns Countryside
links.description: Visitor information for beauty spots and property owned within the Chiltern Hills. Historical estates, geology, wildlife, activities, events, and related links.

links.title: Wikipedia: Chiltern Hills
links.description: Article updated by the public, on the history, geography, geology, protection, associated towns, villages, strip parishes, and the three Chiltern Hundreds, with references and related links.

1054504.title: Clwydian Range and Dee Valley
1054504.description:
The Clwydian Range, formerly Flintshire Range, is a series of hills, highest peak Moel Famau reaching 1818ft / 554m,
east of the Vale of Clwyd, spanning the   Denbighshire and   Flintshire boundary in North Wales,
designated as an area of outstanding natural beauty in 1985.
Since November 2011, the AONB has been extended southwards
into Wrexham Borough, to include   Chirk and the Dee valley westwards to  Llangollen,
encompassing the World Heritage Site,  Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Canal.
The south extension included the town of Corwen, historical landmarks such as Valle Crucis Abbey,
and natural features of Eglwyseg Escarpment, Horseshoe Pass and Esclusham Mountain.

links.title: Clwydian Range and Dee Valley AONB
links.description: Official information for visitors on the 35km chain of heather clad hills and limestone cliffs form one of only 8 protected landscapes in Wales, the southern extension. Includes activities, projects, events, and news blog.

links.title: Moel Famau
links.description: Blog for walkers in the Clwydian Range, featuring the remains of Jubilee Tower hill fort. Includes photos and news for thw summit on the boundary of Flintshire in Denbighshire, north of Llanferres.

links.title: Visit Clwydian Range
links.description: Guide for visitors, with activities, local accommodation and businesses, social media links, client login and map of the area.

links.title: Cornwall Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Partnership coordinating the management of landscapes designated throughout the county. Includes team profiles, their roles, research and community projects, photo gallery, resources for visitors, social media links and contacts.

links.title: Wikipedia: Cornwall Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Summary of the twelve designated sites, their management, references and links to articles updated by the public.

1052585.title: Cotswolds
1052585.description:
This category represents the Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty for the Cotswolds which is mainly in the Coltswold District of Gloucestershire,
but spans other districts and the counties of Warwickshire and Wiltshire, based on their national importance
and to protect their inherited character and preserve wildlife habits.

links.title: Cotswolds National Landscape
links.description: Official information on the landscape of special importance. Details of conservation projects, visitor facilities and attractions, news and events, and contact details.

links.title: Wikipedia: Cotswolds
links.description: Article summarising the range of localities encompassed in the name, and explaining the heritage and environmental significance. Includes references and links to related articles.

1061346.title: Cranborne Chase
1061346.description:
This category represents the Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty for Cranborne Chase which spans parts
the counties of northern Dorset, western Hampshire and Wiltshire.

links.title: Cranborne Chase Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Official information on management of 380 square miles surrounding hills overlapping the boundaries of Dorset, Hampshire, Somerset and Wiltshire. Includes their work, publications, parish map, resources for visitors, social media links and contacts for their office in Tollard Royal.

1055982.title: Isles of Scilly
1055982.description: <dt>This category leads to websites about the archipelago of five inhabited islands and rocky islets, </dt><dd>28 miles west of Lands End, its shallow interior sea, and surrounding Atlantic Ocean.</dd><dt>Fauna and fauna includes seabirds, seals and fish, marine life associated tidal rocks and beaches,</dt><dd> as well as sub-tropical inland wildlife.</dd></dl>

links.title: Twitter: Isles of Scilly AONB
links.description: Latest news from the nationally protected marine and landscape.

links.title: Facebook: Isles of Scilly Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Events requiring login for participation, with links to groups for the islands' wildlife trust and Community Archaeology Group.

1054104.title: Lleyn Peninsula
1054104.description:
This category is for websites relating to the parts of Lleyn Peninsula (Llŷn Peninsula) that have been designated as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty,
extending south of the Isle of Angelsey into the Irish Sea, west from  Caernarfon and  Porthmadog.

links.title: Wikipedia: Llŷn Peninsula
links.description: Article updated by the public, about the history of area, geology, Lleyn sheep breed, nature reserve at Cors Geirch, Coastline and Marine Special Area of Conservation, with 20 Sites of Special Scientific Interest. Includes constituent parishes, and links to related articles.

links.title: Llŷn Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Official information about heritage, conservation of the landscape and wildlife in the area. Includes guide for visitors [English/Welsh].

links.title: Pen Llŷn a’r Sarnau Special Conservation Area
links.description: Protected marine environment off the penisula. Includes indigenous species, map, videos, educational resources and involvemnt such as sightings. [English/Welsh]

links.title: Nefyn landslide, Lleyn Peninsula
links.description: Article about the coastal landslide in January 2001, citing geology, seepage erosion and record rainfall. Includes references from the British Geological Survey.

1060335.title: Norfolk Coast
1060335.description:
This category lists scientific websites for the protected landscape, designated in 1968 to include coastal beaches, sand dunes, salt marshes and cliffs stretching from The Wash at  Hunstanton to  Winterton-on-Sea on the east coast.
The landscape includes nature reserves, particularly for migrating birds, and in some cases this stretched inland to what is now claimed for agriculture.

links.title: Norfolk Coast Protected Landscape
links.description: Describes the landscape, wildlife and heritage of the area, with information about conservation, and for visitors. Includes interactive map for visitors, and xase studoies of cooperation with businesses.

links.title: Wikipedia: Norfolk Coast AONB
links.description: Article introducing the area, and the challenges faced by climate and erosion, with references and links to localities and related articles.

links.title: North Wessex Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Describes the landscape, wildlife and heritage of the area, with information about conservation, and for visitors.

1064441.title: Quantock Hills
1064441.description: Ancient wooded valley landscape, including ash-hazel, western sessile oak, coniferous plantation and small farm woodlands, between Bridgewater, Bishops Lydeard and Williton, towards the north coast of Somerset.    ​

links.title: Quantock Online
links.description: Information about the Quantock Hills, England's first designated Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Covers local business, tourist information and news and events.

links.title: Quantock Hills AONB
links.description: Official information on landscape planning, access management, habitats, coastal geology, activities, events, volunteering, publications and contacts.

links.title: Solway Coast AONB
links.description: Official description of the landscape, wildlife and heritage of the area, with information about conservation, and for visitors.

links.title: Facebook: Solway AONB
links.description: Recent news of sitings and volunteer projects, with photographs and comments from officers and visitors. [requires login to comment]

links.title: Wikipedia: Solway Coast
links.description: Article showing the extent of the AONB along the south coast of the Solway Firth from the mouth of the Eden. Includes a summary of their centre at Silloth-on-Solway, fauna, flora, and perceived threats, with references and related links.

links.title: Silloth's Management Plan for Solway Coast AONB
links.description: Agreement by Allerdale Borough Council’s executive committee to commit to a five-year plan.

811774.title: Jurassic Coast
811774.description: Lyme Regis is located in Dorset, England. The cliffs at Lyme Regis are composed of sediment deposited during the Jurassic, and have yielded marine fossils such as ammonoids and spectacular marine reptiles.  The fossils of Lyme Regis fired the imagination of some of the earliest palaeontologists, and the site continues to amaze and delight fossil collectors.  This location, with the surrounding coast of Devon and Dorset, has recently been accepted as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This distinction is expected to greatly increase the number of visitors with a geological interest to the area.

links.title: Mary Anning
links.description: Short biography of Lyme Regis's most famous fossil hunter.

links.title: Jurassic Coast
links.description: Official guide to England's first UNESCO natural World Heritage Site, along ninety five miles of coastline from East Devon to Dorset. Includes history from the Triassic period, with present-day management and local access.

links.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Dorset and East Devon Coast
links.description: Selected for its coastal topography, and fossils in sequence of rock formations spanning the Mesozoic Era, or millions of years of the earth's history, contributing to earth sciences for over 300 years. Includes description, video, case study, related links, news and events.

links.title: Geology of the Wessex Coast of Southern England
links.description: Ian West provides photographs and information from geological field studies, with links to their localities.

1061035.title: Chesil Beach
1061035.description:
Chisel Beach is a ridge topped with shingle stretching from  West Bay, where it is at the foot of East Cliff, then
to the west leaves the cliffs forming an arch as it reaches the  Isle of Portland.
Chisel Beach appears to be a barrier formed from the sea bed by south westerly tidal surges which is occasionally
over-topped, notably the hurricane of November 1824, and storm surge of 13th February 1978.
A natural tombola joins Portland with the mainland at  Weymouth, which had natural lower points than Chisel Beach,
and has been widened and dredged to form a permanent entrance under Ferry Bridge from Portland Harbour,
ensuring that Fleet Lagoon, remains tidal, providing sheltered marine environment between Chisel Beach and
the undulating coastline back ten miles to  Abbotsbury where Chisel Beach leaves the original coastline.

links.title: Chesil Beach
links.description: Guide to Fleet Lagoon and the barrier beach, with information on history and wildlife, photo gallery, indexed topics, advice on access and some activities available.

links.title: Chesil Beach, Dorset
links.description: Guide illustrated by photographs through the years, describing layers of ages behind the lagoon and geomorphology of ridges in the beach. Includes annotated geological map showing the combinations of clays and marble, presented by Dr Ian West at Southampton University.

links.title: JNCC SAC: Chesil and the Fleet
links.description: Lists the criteria that were satisfied to be designated Special Area of Conservation. Includes PDF downloads of information sheet on Ramsar Wetlands and Natura 2000 on conservation of wild birds.

links.title: Ramsar Sites Information Service: Chesil Beach & The Fleet
links.description: Satellite view of the area, with specifocations for international geomorphologic importance of the wetland resource, and related links.

1059754.title: Reclamation
1059754.description: <dl><dt>This category leads to websites about the parts of the UK that have been reclaimed from </dt><dd>either the sea or marshland that has been drained.</dd><dt>This category also includes websites about proposals to reclaim land, and protect land from flooding </dt><dd>by barriers for rising sea levels [until there is a separate category linked from here].</dd><dt>Where there is an area that is relevant to more than one Locality in the UK, or the Top of the Directory</dt><dd>a subcategory here can been used to link them.</dd><dt>These subcategories may include links to locality categories that have Land Reclamation businesses. </dt><dd> </dd></dl>

links.title: Internal Drainage Board - Bedford Group
links.description: Provides local flood defence in Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire. List of projects and personnel.

links.title: Association of Drainage Authorities
links.description: ADA oversees activities and future actions for ten branches, the Environment Agency, the Regional Flood and Coastal Committees, and member local authorities. Includes emergency planning, meeting records, events, conatcts based at Stoneleigh.

links.title: Water Level Management
links.description: Consortium managing drainage from the catchments of the River Trent from Nottinghamshire to the Humber, and Eastern Lincolnshire. Includes area map covered by three boards, governance, range of services, current works, and contacts headquartered in Manby.

1059327.title: Isle of Axholme
1059327.description:
This category leads to websites for the North Lincolnshire district of the Isle of Axholme,
on the west bank of the River Trent.

The area to the north west of the Isle of Axholme are in the Twin Rivers parish, of the  East Riding of Yorkshire east of  Goole.
If you do not see categories for hamlets such as
Amcotts, Eastoft, Fockerby, Garthopre and Luddington, we await
until there are sufficient websites for a separate category, for the west bank of the Trent.

links.title: IoA & HC Landscape Partnership
links.description: Heritage Lottery funded to manage the distinctive landscape, propducing a leaflet for children, Includes team profile, resources, projects, reports, volunteering, event calendar, and contacts.

1060281.title: Somerset Levels
1060281.description:
This category lists websites for the area inland from Bridgewater Bay, corresponding to land at or near
sea level marshland frequently flooded in winter until its manual drainage at strategically positioned pumping stations.
Natural rivers are the Parrett with its mouth at  Bridgewater,
and the Brue with its mouth at Highbridge and  Burnham-on-Sea.
The Huntspill River is a man-made drain, constructed in 1940, with a pumping station taking water from the Brue
east of  Street and controlling levels according to the tide in the mouth of the Parrett, with a sluice west of  Huntspill.

links.title: Avalon Marshes Landscape Partnership
links.description: Promoting habitat, wildlife, and heritage. Includes articles on nature reserves, volunteering, events diary, links and contacts for related organisations.

1060279.title: The Fens
1060279.description:
This category lists websites for the area inland from The Wash, corresponding to marshland frequently flooded
in winter until their manual drainage at strategically positioned pumping stations.
This dates back to Roman hydraulics, and there are traces of medieval drainage works, but major reclamation
for agriculture was during the seventeenth century, with drainage maintained by windpumps.
The Fens drain into the Wash at the mouths of
The Great Ouse at  King's Lynn, Norfolk,
The River Nene at  Sutton Bridge, South Holland,
The River Welland at  Fosdyke, and Haven at  Boston, Lincolnshire.
The major open drains join the Great Ouse in Cambridgeshire;
the Old and New Bedford Rivers, also known as the Hundred Foot Drain, from  Earith in Cambridgeshire.

links.title: Gov.UK Countryside Stewardship: The Fens
links.description: Resources describing the history and geography of the area, mainly below 10 m above the level, which prior to pumped drainage and controlled sluices, was marshland. Includes priorities, advice and maps.

links.title: Nene Valley Archaeological Trust
links.description: Professional archaeologists and local amateur groups combine to discover, document and communicate the area's history. Includes records of digs since 1957, publications on Roman pottery, prehistoric and medieval artefacts, and news blog.

links.title: Wicken Fen
links.description: Details on this nature reserve of the ancient fenland landscape, owned by the National Trust. Features reed-bed, wet woodland and open water, on peat soil kept wet by rainfall and chalky river water straddling Bedfordshire and Cambridgeshire.

links.title: Fens for the Future
links.description: Partnership aiming to extend existing waterways and wetland to establish a sustainable ecosystem and water storage network across Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.

links.title: Devil’s Dyke
links.description: Blog about the Anglo-Saxon earthwork running between the villages of Reach and Woodditton. Includes native flora and fauna, photo galleries, bird sound recordings, map, visitor information and related links.

links.title: Prickwillow Museum
links.description: Collection of estored diesel engines used for the drainage of the Fens, history of the area, the people involved, camparison with wind and steam, information for visitors, blog , links to videos and contacts.

links.title: Great Fen
links.description: Project started in 2001 to restore and manage a 2140 acre wetland area between Peterborough and Huntingdon, for the benefit of wildlife and amenity. Includes bird migration, sightings, invertebrate, mammals and plants galleries, educational resources, visitor information, events, news blog, and contacts.

links.title: GLNP: South Lincolnshire Fenlands Partnership
links.description: Introduction to restoration aims, to re-create up to 800 hectares of lost wild fenlands between Bourne and Market Deeping. Includes Wildlife Trust reserves, objectives regarding agriculture, reedbeds, swampland, wet woodlands and wildlife.

links.title: Lost Skills of  Fenland Folk
links.description: Story of the last of the fen tigers, an endangered folk of the eastern fenlands, river people who earned an often precarious living in wetlands.

links.title: Black Sluice Internal Drainage Board: Map of District
links.description: Interactive display of the low lying fens south and west of Boston, showing the system for pumping rainwater into the River Witham , and the sluiced Haven, for realease at low tide in the Wash.

links.title: Wikipedia: Cambridgeshire Lodes
links.description: Article contributed by the public, describing the series of man-made waterways, originated in the Roman era, draining into the River Cam, leading via the River Great Ouse, to the Wash. Includes history, plan with current pumping stations, locks and sluices, references and related links.

links.title: Must Farm
links.description: Discovery commecrcial transport in the River Nene in 2011, and archeological excavation of a Bronze Age settlement from 2015 to 2016. Includes dig diaries, FAQ, future plans.

links.title: BBC Radio 4: The Fens: Discovering England's Ancient Depths
links.description: Radio series of five 15-minute programmes narrated by Dr Francis Pryor, featuring archeaological research on Bronze Age settlements from Fengate to Musk Farm before the influx of sea from the Wash and sedimentation. Progresses to present day speculation.

531221.title: Waste and Recycling
531221.description: Recycling involves processing used materials into new products to prevent waste of potentially useful materials and reduce the consumption of fresh raw materials.

links.title: Enlightened Lamp Recycling Ltd
links.description: Company based in Redhill, Surrey specialising in the treatment and recycling of fluorescent lamps, mercury and other hazardous waste, with a national collect and recycle service.

links.title: Recycling & Waste World
links.description: Magazine published weekly providing a source of information for the UK recycling and waste management industry.

links.title: WRAP
links.description: Organisation helping businesses and individuals reduce waste, develop sustainable products and use resources in an efficient way. The focus is on packaging, food waste, local authority collection and recycling systems.

links.title: GreenBoxDay
links.description: Offers to remind users by email or text to put our their recycling and other household waste on the correct day for collection by their local council.

links.title: Recycle Now
links.description: Advice and ideas on recycling. Aims to promote recycling through campaigns.

links.title: RECOUP
links.description: National charity aiming to maximise plastics recycling in the UK, promote best practices and provide educational and training tools.

links.title: Recyclezone
links.description: Educational site dealing with the 3Rs; reduce, reuse and recycle. Besides information, it provides fun, activity, recycler and teacher zones.

links.title: Recycling Guide
links.description: Provides tips and advice on how to recycle almost anyything. Includes news and readers' comments.

links.title: Giv UK: Waste and Recycling
links.description: Provides news and information on waste in the UK, strategy, legislation, what happens to it, controls and permits, and information for local authorities.

links.title: Resource Futures
links.description: Waste consultancy. Includes details of services, public sector and commercial projects, education and assisting charitable organisations.

links.title: Recycle-More
links.description: Gives recycling information for business, schools and consumers.

links.title: Freecycle
links.description: Matches people who have things they want to get rid of with people who can use them, keeping usable items out of landfills. Local group search, explanation and etiquette.

links.title: Letsrecycle.com
links.description: Recycling and waste management news and information

links.title: P V Surveys Ltd
links.description: Provide asbestos surveys locally in London, Sussex, Kent, Essex and nationally across the UK also offers training. Includes overview, services and meet the team.

links.title: Industry Council for Electronic Equipment Recycling
links.description: An association of member companies dealing with the recycling or treatment of waste from electrical and electronic equipment.

links.title: Edinburgh International Science Festival
links.description: Annual event in early April includes events and shows relating to science and technology. Features exhibitions, workshops, tours, talks, demonstrations and hands-on activities, all aimed at the general public.

links.title: Orkney International Science Festival
links.description: Describes this annual event, with programme details, information for schools and visitors, photographs, and forum. Orkney Islands, Scotland.

links.title: Science Museum
links.description: London museum and library of science. Exhibitions cover all areas of science and technology. Includes online exhibits and a learning area.

links.title: Magna Science Adventure Centre
links.description: Collection includes architecture, aviation, design, industry, natural sciences, science and technology plus social history. Rotherham, South Yorkshire.

links.title: Museum of the History of Science, University of Oxford
links.description: Exhibiting the history of science. Online exhibits include "The Noble Dane: Images of Tycho Brahe" and "The Geometry of War, 1500-1750".

links.title: Catalyst
links.description: Science centre and museum devoted to chemistry and how the products of chemistry are used in every day life. Widnes, Cheshire.

links.title: Whipple Museum of the History of Science
links.description: Science and its applications from physics to phrenology and from magnetism to microscopy. Scientific instruments, models, prints, books, and related objects. Cambridge.

links.title: The Observatory Science Centre
links.description: Hands-on science among the domes and telescopes of the former Royal Greenwich Observatory. Herstmonceux, East Sussex.

links.title: Thinktank
links.description: Museum of science and discovery, with business venue facilities and an IMAX cinema. Includes information about exhibits and online booking. Birmingham.

links.title: The Natural History Museum
links.description: The national museum of natural history. Major research and teaching collections cover botany, entomology, mineralogy, palaeontology and zoology, mainly from the 18th and early 19th centuries. Online tour of the galleries. London

links.title: The Old Operating Theatre Museum  and Herb Garret
links.description: Britain's oldest surviving operating theatre. Provides history of the museum, details of its facilities, schools and groups. London.

links.title: Museum of Victorian Science
links.description: Features a virtual tour of Dr. Frankenstein's laboratory, display of working Geissler, Bouquet, Railway and early x-ray tubes, and electric flame-laden demonstrations.  Visits by appointment only. Includes directions.  Located in North Yorkshire, United Kingdom.

links.title: The Freud Museum of London
links.description: The London home of Sigmund and his daughter Anna Freud. Now a museum containing Freud's library, and his collection of antiquities.

links.title: The Manchester Museum
links.description: International collection of natural history artefacts. Newly opened aquarium and vivarium. Site of first international Mummy Tissue Bank.

links.title: National Space Science Centre
links.description: Space museum and discovery centre in Leicester. Ticket and booking details. Site map and attraction information.

links.title: Life
links.description: Brings together science and biotechnology, research and education, entertainment and ethics. Newcastle upon Tyne.

links.title: South Downs Planetarium
links.description: Seats 100 people.  Created to promote a greater public understanding of science and to encourage more young people to take up science as a career. Chichester.

links.title: The Museum of Science & Industry
links.description: Virtual exhibits on everything from locomotives and aircrafts, to photography and nuclear power. Lists exhibitions, collections, events and contacts in Manchester.

links.title: The Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery, University of Glasgow
links.description: Collection and web images include rocks and minerals, zoological specimens, human anatomical collection, coins and medals.

links.title: Glasgow Science Centre
links.description: Hands-on exhibits, science theatre and planetarium. Visitor details and calendar.

links.title: Jodrell Bank Visitor Centre
links.description: Visitor details for the Lovell Radio Telescope and the Jodrell Bank Observatory, the astronomy research centre of the University of Manchester. Cheshire.

links.title: Cambridge Museum of Technology
links.description: Preserved Victorian pumping station. Includes functional steam engines and historical engineering items.

links.title: London Museum of Water & Steam
links.description: Collection of giant pumping engines in a Victorian waterworks on the Thames, and the history of water supply. Description of the major exhibits and visitor information. London.

links.title: The Museum of Power
links.description: Overview and pictures of the museum dedicated to all forms of power, from steam to electric, housed in the Steam Pumping Station at Langford in Essex.

links.title: Westonzoyland Pumping Station
links.description: Museum of stationary steam engines and land drainage history of the Somerset Levels, at the county's oldest surviving pumping station. Includes details of location, opening times, exhibited engines and how to support their work.

links.title: The Claymills Pumping Engines Trust
links.description: Society preserving and restoring the steam powered pumping station at Clay Mills, near Burton Upon Trent in Staffordshire. Archives, technical data, online tour and visitor information with dates for next steaming.

links.title: Ironbridge Gorge Museums
links.description: The Shropshire site of the birth of the Industrial Revolution has been designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. Visitor information and a virtual tour.

links.title: Bletchley Park - Station X
links.description: World War ll codebreaking centre and home of Colossus, the world’s first semi-programmable computer . Visitor information, news, events and the work of the trust. Bletchley, Buckinghamshire.

links.title: Royal Gunpowder Mills, Waltham Abbey
links.description: Open to the public for the first time in 300 years, summer only. Exhibitions on the history of explosives, wildlife and the restoration of a narrow gauge railway. Essex.

links.title: Ferguson Family Museum
links.description: Isle of Wight. Museum recording the life and interests of an inventor known for his tractor. Includes biography, information on his monoplane, plough, three point linkage, and tractors, map and contact details.

links.title: The National Museum of Computing
links.description: Aims to collect and restore computer systems developed in Britain. Exhibits include Colossus, built in 1943. Visitor information, virtual tour, events, news and shop.

links.title: National Brewery Centre
links.description: Brewing collection, including historic equipment, transportation vehicles, pub memorabilia and advertising materials. Location and details of exhibits.

links.title: New Scientist
links.description: Science and technology news from the weekly magazine includes daily updates from around the world. Includes Hot Topics, interviews, book reviews and job listings.

links.title: Ecologist
links.description: Comment, blogs and investigations on key environmental and climate change issues plus green living advice.

links.title: BBC Science & Nature
links.description: Information about humans, animals, space, the planet Earth and various hot topics. Includes TV listings, Listen Again online radio, news reports, quizzes, picture galleries and games.

links.title: Permanent Publications
links.description: Subscription information for Permaculture Magazine and a catalogue of available books, videos, and other resources.

links.title: Telegraph: Science and Technology
links.description: Includes the latest news plus regular columnists, features, competitions and computer book reviews.

links.title: BBC News - Technology
links.description: News and features including e-commerce, digital media and gaming.

links.title: ENDS Report
links.description: Provides environmental intelligence for professionals including a directory of environmental consultancies with capabilities, qualifications and experience.

links.title: BBC News: Science and Environment
links.description: Offers news and feature stories plus audio and video programmes and clips.

links.title: The Guardian - Environment
links.description: News and features about the global environment with sections on climate change, conservation, travel, energy, ethical living, food, water and pollution. Includes regular columnists, campaigns and how to get involved.

links.title: The Guardian - Science
links.description: Latest news and information including a weekly podcast, opinions, analysis and background from the Guardian and Observer newspapers plus special reports, interactive guides and talkboards.

links.title: The Guardian - Technology
links.description: News and features about the internet and technology. Includes business solutions, science news, e-issues and special reports plus web watch, gadgets, games, blogs and Ask Jack.

links.title: Science Media Centre
links.description: Works to promote the voices, stories and views of the UK scientific community to the news media when science is in the headlines.

links.title: The British Academy
links.description: Spans the humanities and social sciences. Fellowship information, publications, meetings, research funding and reports, other resources.

links.title: The Royal Institution of Great Britain
links.description: Information on website includes history of the institution, its buildings, current activities.

links.title: Science and Engineering Experiments for Kids
links.description: Organisation based at the University of Cambridge, whose aim is to promote the excitement and fun of science and engineering to children in primary schools using hands-on experiments.

links.title: The Fairyland Trust
links.description: Aims to encourage conservation by helping children discover nature's magic. Details of fairy fairs, activities and workshops, a fairy places gazetteer, plus information on how to build a magical garden and how to contribute to the charity.

links.title: Sustainable Consumption Institute (The University of Manchester)
links.description: Multidisciplinary centre of global excellence researching major national and international issues associated with sustainability in the retail sector and encouraging consumers to adopt more sustainable lifestyles.

links.title: British Entomology and Natural History Society
links.description: Provides information on membership, the journal, other publications, grants, research and the collecting code.

links.title: Association of Applied Biologists
links.description: Aims to promote the study of all branches of biology and to foster the practice, growth and development of applied biology. Provides information on publications, conferences and membership.

links.title: Chartered Institution of Water and Environmental Management
links.description: Professional and examining body for scientists, engineers and other environmental professionals committed to the sustainable management and development of water and the environment.  Includes publications, branches and events.

links.title: Royal Microscopical Society
links.description: The Society aims to advance science, develop careers and support wider understanding of science and microscopy. Information on membership, news and events, and publishes the Journal of Microscopy.

links.title: Institution of Environmental Sciences (IES)
links.description: Group aims to raise public awareness of environmental science by supporting professional scientists and academics working in this field. Includes information on membership, news, events, continuing professional development, awards and resources.

links.title: Institute of Environmental Management and Assessment
links.description: IEMA is an organisation established to promote best practice standards in environmental management, auditing and assessment. Includes information on membership, training, regions, events and publications.

links.title: Environmental Research Institute
links.description: Organisation undertaking research into a range of environmental topics. Includes news, education, facilities and staff.

links.title: Field Studies Council

1052952.title: Britannia Bridge
1052952.description:
This category is for websites about Robert Stephenson's tubular iron rail bridge opened in 1850, and the steel arch bridge built on the same site following fire damage in 1970.
The span is over the Menai Strait to the west of Bangor, to the Anglesey town of Llanfairpwllgwyngyll.
The newer bridge is two tier and carries the railway into the town centre, whereas the upper tier carries the A55 trunk road from the south west of Bangor, and a ring road around the north of Llanfairpwllgwyngyll, connecting the Welsh mainland with Anglesey, and onward to the Irish Sea ferry at Holyhead.

:

1059447.description:

It spans the Avon Gorge from Bristol to North Somerset.
Traffic is now dwarfed by the M5 over the mouth of the Avon, and the A370 into the city centre at lower ground.

1059440.title: Humber Bridge
1059440.description:
This category lists websites about the Humber Bridge, opened to road traffic in 1981,
and until 1998 was the longest suspension bridge in the world.
It spans the estuary of the Rivers Ouse and Trent before the Humber enters the  North Sea,
and joins the A15 from Lincoln via the M180 to  East Riding of Yorkshire.
Before rising over the Humber, the A15 by-passes  Barton-upon-Humber.
The northern tower meets the East Riding of Yorkshire at  Hessle.
The latter location serves as a means of revenue housing toll booths.

1054159.title: London Bridge
1054159.description:
This category is for websites about the first bridge to cross the River Thames from The City of London to Southwark on the south bank.
This dates back to Roman times from AD43, though this category lists websites to the bridges called London Bridge, that replaced this on the same site between present day bridges upstream at Southwark, and down stream at the Tower of London;  Tower Bridge.
The present day London Bridge was opened to road traffic in 1974, after its predecessor from 1830 was dismantled to be
rebuilt in Lake Havasu City, Arizona, which had in turn replaced a 600-year-old medieval multiple arch structure, including gateways and houses.

1052964.title: Royal Albert Bridge
1052964.description:
This category is for websites about the iron railway bridge dedicated to Victoria's Prince Albert, designed by I K Brunel, and opened just before his death 1859.
It was designed to span the tidal estuary of the Tamar, providing a 30m. clearance at high tide for naval ships.
The design predates the Through Arch types, since the wrought iron arch starts after beams on multiple stone pillar approaches, and the deck is kept level throughout with support of a single tubular arch, rising over the level deck throughout the span.
The bridge is also known as Saltash Bridge, since from Plymouth the first station on the west bank, and town is Saltash in Cornwall.

1053561.title: Canals
1053561.description: <dl><dt>This category leads to websites about canals in the British Isles, originally built as a form of Transport at the beginning of the Industrial Revolution, to serve as a Water Resource for emerging Technology.</dt><dt>At the time Canals would have been regarded as Technology, undertaken by Civil Engineers, to control water, from a source higher than the level of the Canal, so that canal boats could be lifted at locks, by trapping water escaping by gravity, until sufficient water was collected in the water to be level with the canal above, then progress along level water until the next lock.</dt><dt>With the advent of the Railways, some canal construction was never completed, such as with the plans to join the mouth of the Severn with the English Channel, The Grand Western Canal.</dt><dt>Railways were largely superseded by road transport, as the most convenient means of transporting goods, and many canals were culverted rather than constructing road bridges under which canal traffic could continue.  </dt><dt>In both these cases the non-navigable canal became a Water Resource for Course Fishing, and local recreation such as canoeing.</dt><dt>Neglected canals, became a Water Resource for Wildlife, and because of their towpaths, canals provided recreational Water Resources, such as Walking and Cycling.</dt><dt>In some cases the canal locks and technological heritage provide a tourist attraction, most notable the World Heritage Site of Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, on the Langollen Canal.</dt><dt>Although the industrial significance of British canals had its hay day, during the latter part of the nineteenth century the heritage canals were recognised locally as a Water Resource for Tourism, particularly recreational narrow boats, and many culverted sections were reopened by providing bridges under which narrow boats could pass, such as The Rochdale Leeds Canal over the Pennines.</dt><dt>Sites listed here should contain scientific information about Canals as a Water Resource, whether   the Technology behind their construction for the Industrial Revolution, providing an Ecological Niche for wildlife, or resource for future technology such as hydro electric power.</dt><dt>This category may contain subcategories about a specific canal where sufficient websites justify this,whereas some categories have already been created recognising the Recreational or Tourism aspects, and  have been linked from here.</dt></dl>

links.title: CanalPlanAC
links.description: Waterway route planning, for boat trips or holidays along the rivers and canals. Includes distances between locks, photos of places, and views of sections from maps.

links.title: Birmingham Canal Navigation Society
links.description: BCNS aims to conserve, restore, iimprove and encourage interests in the 100 mile network of the Birmingham and Black Country. Includes history, aims, guide for moorings and facilities, cruises, blog and archive of events, map of locations, social media links, and membership contacts.

links.title: Kent and East Sussex Canal Restoration Group
links.description: KESCRG is a volunteer restoration movement offering work camps since 1983. Includes history and dig reports from other parts of the country.

1054048.title: Llangollen and Pontcysyllte Aqueduct
1054048.description:
This category is for websites about the UNESCO World Heritage Site, named Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Canal, featuring Telford's multiple arch aqueduct across the Dee Valley between villages of   ‎Froncysyllte and Trevor on the west boundary of the County Borough of Wrexham, before following the north bank of the River Dee upstream to its source north of Llangollen.
The Llangollen Canal has another aqueduct downstream, across the River Ceiriog on the south boundary of Wrexham Borough Council at  Chirk. 
This category includes websites about this aqueduct and the 18km of the Llangollen Canal, before entering the Shropshire Canal.

links.title: Wikipedia: Llangollen Canal
links.description: Article updated by the public about the history, decline and restoration of navigation to the Shropshire Union Canal. Includes route plan, references and links to related articles.

links.title: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct
links.description: Visitor Centre with information for tour planning, community organisations, diary, news with social media links, and contacts at Trevor Basin.

links.title: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Cefn Viaduct
links.description: Group reinstating the Plas Kynaston Canal back to Cefn Mawr at the center of the World Heritage.

links.title: Wikipedia: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct
links.description: Illustrated article updated by the public, featuring the history and construction of structure, with references and links to related articles.

links.title: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct World Heritage Site
links.description: Introduction to the World Heritage Site stretching 11 miles along the Llangollen Canal from the Hoseshoe Falls above Llangollen to Gledrid Bridge past Chirk.

1054093.title: Montgomery Canal
1054093.description:
This category lists websites for the extension of the Shropshire Union Canal, now known as the Montgomery Canal, originally constructed as the Montgomeryshire Canal, and does not pass through this town.
The original destination was to  Newtown, but construction ceased at Garthmyl, and following breach in 1936, the Western branch fell into disuse, with restoration only comparatively recent.  The canal is currently isolated from the Shropshire Union Canal, and navigable only for 7 miles between Frankton Junction to Gronwyn Wharf, and a section at Llanymynech around Welshpool.

links.title: Montgomery Canal Restoration
links.description: Details of project to improve naviagtion, including events, reports of working party dates with photos, and connectrions with the Shropshire Union Canal Society.

links.title: Coflein: Berriew Aqueduct, Montgomeryshire Canal
links.description: Introduction to the history and construction, with maps and archived timeline, from the Royal Commission on the ancient and historical monuments of Wales.

links.title: Victorian Powys: Montgomeryshire Canal
links.description: Historical article featuring the aqueducts over the Rivers Vyrnwy and Rhiw at Berriew.

links.title: The Archaeology of the Montgomeryshire Canal by Stephen Hughes
links.description: Copy of some book pages from The Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales. Includes hyperlinked contents and index, illustrations include diagram of construction, with links for purchase.

links.title: Canal Plan AC: Freeestone Lock
links.description: Limit of current navigation between Welshpool and Newtown. Includes links to information and facilities in the area.

links.title: Wikipedia: Montgomery Canal
links.description: Article updated by the public about the history, and renaming despite the canal never passing the town of Montgomery. Includes limits of navigation, restoration, nature conservation, route plan, references and links to related articles.

1052432.title: Lakes and Lochs
1052432.description:
This category leads to geographical websites devoted to inland lakes and lochs, within the British Isles.
This refers to the large bodies of non-tidal water throughout the UK, generally Freshwater,
fed from a catchment area of streams and rivers, and flow in to a River leading to the  Sea.
  • Some lakes do not have the word Lake in the official title, particularly in the Cumbrian Lake District,
  • whereas some have Water appended.
  • Loch or Lough are the preferred terms in Scotland.
Not all Lochs and Loughs are freshwater, and to varying degrees may be Marine, such as Stranford Lough in
Northern Ireland, and the ecology may be regarded as Estuarine.

links.title: South West Lakes Trust: Lakes
links.description: Conservation and leisure charity in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset and Somerset. Information on the locations, operations, facilities, activities, services, people and contacts.

1063049.title: Cumbrian Lakes
1063049.description: The southern half of Cumbria is known as The Lake District is the largest of the National Parks, and contains 16 lakes, as well as more than 150 high mountains, 6 National Nature Reserves, 100 sites of Special Scientific Interest, over 50 delectable dales, and hundreds of towns, villages and hamlets within its 885 square miles of breathtaking countryside.

links.title: Ullswater
links.description: The Lake, information about the area, where to stay and things to do. Details of the Ullswater festival.

1063051.title: Lough Neagh
1063051.description:
This category leads to websotes abput Lough Neagh, Northern Ireland,
the largest freshwater lakeby area in the British Isles.

links.title: Wikipedia: Lough Neagh
links.description: Artticle describing the largest by area fresh water lake in the British Isles, its geography, geology and hydrologocal statics. Includes photographs, human history and cureent uses, with references and links to associated settlements.

links.title: Lough Neagh Partnership
links.description: Resources for the lake and its waterways available, including heritage sites, nature, wldlife, beaches, forests, parks, gardens. Includes marina locations and events.

1052975.title: Marine
1052975.description:
This category is for websites specifically about tidal waters off the coast of the United Kingdom of Great Britain, and Northern Ireland.
For recreational use of marine waters, please see  UK: Recreation . . .Water_Sports
and for related businesses:
  UK: Business and Economy: Marine Sales and_Services.

links.title: Tide Times
links.description: Dynamic map, with satellite view, of British Isles showing low and high at coastal sites, from Ireland to Bluemull Sound and the Thames estuary. Including calendars predicting neap, spring,tidal conditions.

links.title: North West Coast Forum
links.description: Partnership of Irish Sea Coast and Estuary Strategies, aiming to promote the sustainable use and integrated management of sustainable fisheries, geology and community demographics around the coast.

links.title: Tidal Energy
links.description: Resource summarising the potential sites and technologies for harnessing tidal power around the British Isles.

links.title: Marinet
links.description: Network of Friends of the Earth campaigning to protect marine environment around the coast of the UK. Includes details of electricity generation projects, and potential consequences.

links.title: The Nautical Institute
links.description: Non-governmental organisation with consultative status at the International Maritime Organisation, representing seafarers and maritime professionals. Includes membership, events, social media links, and contacts for their office in London.

links.title: East Anglian Coastal Group
links.description: Intitially based upon the coast from the Wash to the River Thames, extended in 1989 to cover the Environment Agency coastline from the Humber to the Thames. Includes management aims, and coastal defence policy development with DEFRA.

1060203.title: Humber
1060203.description:
This category leads to websites about the marine inlet, between  Lincolnshire
and the  East Riding of Yorkshire on the east coast of England.
The Humber starts in the west at the confluence of two major rivers.
The mouth of the River Ouse meanders around the East Yorkshire port of  Goole.
The mouth of the  River Trent exits North Lincolnshire at  Alkborough.
The Humber is crossed by road traffic only at the Ouse Bridge on the M62 motoraway, or the suspension bridge between  Barton-upon-Humber and  Hessle,
by the  Humber Bridge.
To the east, the Humber becomes the Mouth of the Humber, which leads to the  North Sea, between the sandspit known as Spurn Head, south east of the
village of  Easington and the coastal resort of  Humberston in North East Lincolnshire.

links.title: Associated British Ports Humber Estuary Services
links.description: Information about the Rivers Humber, Ouse and Trent for commercial and leisure information users, including pilotage, tidal, navigation and statutary information.

links.title: Humber Pilots
links.description: History of pilotage, an account and documentation of the pilots' cooperative, with related links and contacts in Kirk Ella.

links.title: Wikipedia: Humber
links.description: Article describing the estuary, crossings, with photographs, references and related links on the geography and ecology.

links.title: GLNP: Humber Management Scheme
links.description: The Humber Management Scheme (HMS) provides a coordinated and joined up approach for the management of the Humber Estuary European Marine Site (EMS).

links.title: Strangford Lough & Lecale Partnership
links.description: Information on the topography, culture, marine life and conservation. Calendar of events, including presentations on migration of conger eel, arctic tern and brent goose.

links.title: Wikipedia: Strangford Lough
links.description: Article about the sea inlet, including the calcareous algae and tidal energy generation project.

links.title: Guardian: Tidal Power Comes to Northern Ireland
links.description: National newspaper article on the installation of Seagen, claiming to be the world's first commercial scale tidal stream energy generator, with two rotating blades, 43m wide, that turn at 14 revolutions per minute.

links.title: Northern Ireland News: Strangford Lough Turbine to Power-up at Easter
National Trust: Strangford Lough
links.description: Hiostory of the internationally important landscape, farming, wildlife around its shores, bird migration, volunteering, and information for visitors.

links.title: Walk NI: Strangford Lough
links.description: Resource for walkers around the shores, with photo gallleries of landscape organised in separate trails. Include pounts of interest, facilities and policy for visitors.

links.title: BBC Tide Tables: Strangford
links.description: Tool to plan plan for high and low tides, with links to weather forecasts,

1010609.title: The Wash
1010609.description:
This category lists scientific websites for the tidal bay and estuary fed by the rivers,
Great Ouse, Nene, Welland and Witham.
The boundary with the North Sea is between  Hunstanton in Norfolk, and Gibraltar Point, south of  Skegness in Lincolnhire.
The Wash is a significant habitat for resident wader and migrating sea birds, and has
come under threat for technology such as electricity generation.

links.title: Wikipedia: The Wash
links.description: Introductory article explainnig the geography, history, water temperature, birds and marine life and proposed uses, with references and links to related topics.

links.title: Wash Wader Ringing Group
links.description: Since 1959, aiming to gain understanding of the species of birds, operating around the shores with cannon nets and mist nets. Includes field work programmes, blog and social media links.

links.title: The Wash National Nature Reserve
links.description: Leaflet originally published by Natural England introducing the protected area, with a map. This now has redundant references and is no longer available from the Government body, but this is held by the WWRG.

1053372.title: Rivers
1053372.description:
This category is for geographical websites devoted to inland streams and rivers, down to their estuaries to the British coast.
ie. for non-tidal rivers, or those that do not have an Estuary category under  Marine.

links.title: UK Rivers Network
links.description: Group encouraging involvement in projects and campaigns to protect and conserve biodiversity of local water habitats throughout the UK and Ireland. Includes educational resources, suggested walks, RSS feed and social media link.

links.title: Environment Agency: Putting Fish on the ‘Highway’ to Success
links.description: Report to coincide with World Fish Migration Day, on the opening over the last four years of obstruction to migrating salmon in England’s rivers.

links.title: Farson Digital Watercams
links.description: Providing views of UK rivers at bridges throughout the UK waterways network. Presents map linking locations, with images updated at 10 second intervals, instructions for additional cameras, FAQ, terms and contact form.

links.title: The River Ribble
links.description: Guide from its source in North Yorkshire, to the sea at Lytham in Lancashire. INcludes photographs of points along the way, linked to maps.

links.title: Gov.UK: Flood Information Service
links.description: Provodes the latest estimates of river levels, in conjunction with marine tides, regularly monitoring by this network.

links.title: The UK Rivers Guidebook
links.description: Forum for reporting conditions primariuly for water sports, for each UK country, with FAQ and reports from Europe and other continents.

links.title: River Levels Snapshot
links.description: Snapshot locations where flow is above normal and riseing, flood Warning summary and five day flooding risk forecast.

1063213.title: Mersey
1063213.description:
This category leads to websites about the River Mersey deriving its name from the  Anglo-Saxon for "boundary river":,
corresponding to Mercia and Northumbria, later between the historic counties of  Lancashire and  Cheshire.
In 1974 the areas on both banks of the lower reaches of the Mersey Estuary and marine mouth, were absorbed into the
metropolitan county of  Merseyside.
The River Mersey is formed with the confluence of the Rivers Goyt and Tame,
now under the M60 and the Peel Centre in  Stockport.
The river winds south of  Manchester, often forming the boundary of this city;  Gatley a suburban area
in the  Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, Greater Manchester, south of  Didsbury
then west of  Chorlton-cum-Hardy,  Sale before entering the  Manchester Ship Canal at  Irlam, then briefly
representing the boundary between  Salford City and  Trafford Borough at  Urmston, Carrinton and  Partington,
and crossed by a bridge at Warburton, to join the A57 to  Warrington in Cheshire,
where the canal is sluiced for the river to flow through the town centre before flowing west where it
becomes estuarine between  Runcorn and  Widnes.
Here the Mersey is spanned by A533 road bridge known as the Mersey Gateway.
A shorter span is west, the A533, Silver Jubilee Bridge, paired with a rail bridge at Runcorn Gap.
At this point the Manchester Ship Canal is still south of the estuary, and between the two road bridges, a lock
serves as transit at high tide, but the main entrance is further west, north west of  Ellesmere Port at locks
in the Merseyside parish of  Eastham.
North of Eastham the mouth of the Mersey forms the metropolitan district boundary between  Liverpool city
and the  Wirral Peninsula.

links.title: Wikipedia: River Mersey
links.description: Guide to the river and estuary, outlining its course, its crossings, navigation, recreation, environmental issues, with references and links to articles on its tributaries.

links.title: Environment Agency: Salmon Behaviour in the Mersey Catchment
links.description: Report of a study into the distribution and upstream movement of Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). Includes maps of routes, tagging methods, observed behaviour, obstacles and failures to reach spawning areas.

1053373.title: Severn
1053373.description: This category is for geographical websites devoted to the longest river in the UK, with its source above the Hafren Forest in North Wales, flowing through the English Midlands and flowing through Gloucestershire, with its tidal bore at its mouth, to the Bristol Channel between England and Wales, spanned by the Severn Suspension Bridge at Cheptow, and the Second Severn Crossing, at Caldicot, where the railway tunnel also emerges.

links.title: Marinenet: Warning to MPs from Wildlife NGOs About the Dangers of a Severn Barrage
links.description: Blog report of House of Commons Energy and Climate Committee considering Hafren Power tidal energy development and claims of imminent ecological damage.

1053411.title: Tamar
1053411.description:
Websites about the river forming the border between Devon and Cornwall for much of its length to Plymouth Sound,
and incorporating Tamar Valley Area of Outstading Natural Beauty.
The most northerly point is the catchment to the man-made Upper Tamar Lake, which the county boundary dissects
between the parishes of  Bradworthy and  Kilkhampton.
Upper Tamar Lake is only five miles from the west coast, and ground water in Kilkhampton flows to the west, so
although the Tamar forms the boundary flowing south, is not regarded as the Tamar Valley.
More tributaries come from the parish of Bradsworthy, although the River Walden through Bradsworthy flows east,
and joins the River Torridge, eventually flowing north into the Barnstaple Bay.
Lower Tamar Lake is entirely within Devon, and from Bradsworthy parish the Tamar flows through Pancrasweek parish,
then again forms the county boundary with Launcells, but then the Tamar is entirely within  Bridgerule,
before separating Whitstone and Pyworthy.
At North Tamerton, the Tamar is joined by the River Deer from Holsworthy, again dividing the counties at
Tetcott, Luffincott, Northcott and St Giles on the Heath in the  Torridge District of Devon.
South of North Tamerton the parishes on the west bank of the Tamar are Boyton and Werrington before  Launceston.
The Tamar remains the county boundary for the West Devon parishes of Lifton, Bradstone, Dunterton,  Milton Abbot, 
Sydenham Damerel, then Gulworthy,  Bere Alston,  Bere Ferrers, where the River Tavy joins the tidal estuary,
with Plymouth on the east bank.  Here bridges span the Tamar to  Saltash.
Upstream from Saltash on the west bank are the Cornish parishes of Botusfleming, Landulph, Pillaton,
St Dominick, Calstock (represented by  Gunnislake), Stoke Climsland, Lezant & Lawhitton, south of Launceston.

links.title: Tamar Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Describes the landscape, wildlife and heritage of the area, with information about conservation, blog and social media link.

links.title: Cornwall Guide: Tamar Bridges
links.description: Introduction to the two bridge crossing from Plymouth to Saltash by rail and road. Includes photos of construction phases, and related images.

links.title: Visit Tamar Valley
links.description: Describes wooded river valley with catchment in Bodmin Moor to Dartmoor, with associated mining heritage, sailing, canoeing, fishing, and visitor information.

links.title: YouTube: River Tamar
links.description: Video from the early 1980's BBC documentary by Peter Purves, interviewing farmers and locals. Includes links to related videos.

links.title: Tamar Trails Centre
links.description: Outdoor activities available including those organised for groups as well as individual visitors. Includes calendar of events, photo gallery, news blog and link to video.

links.title: Tamar Valley Line
links.description: Railway between Plymouth up the east bank of the river, leaving Devon at Calstock to Gunnislake in Cornwall. Map and excursion guide.

links.title: Devon County Council: Middle Tamar Valley
links.description: Formal description of the landscape character types, distinctions, characteristics, evaluation and conservation strategy.

links.title: Walks around The Tamar Valley
links.description: Details of planned 3 to 5 mile walks around the area, with directions, maps, photos and information about the places of interest along the routes.

links.title: River Tamar Project
links.description: Cultural programme, connecting local and international communities to preserve the memories of the river, through art and education. Includes team profile, history, sponsors and social media links.

links.title: Wikipedia: River Tamar
links.description: Article updated by the public on derivation of name, navigation history, geographical and environmental features, with table of crossings, references, and links to related articles.

links.title: Cornishlight:River Tamar
links.description: Photographs featuring bridges spanning the river dividing Devon and Cornwall.

links.title: SW Lakes Trust: Tamar Lakes
links.description: Introduction to the recreational facilities at two gravity dams Upper and Lower, whose catchment form the source of the river, east of Kilkhampton, separated by the bridge between Thurdon, Cornwall and Alfisworthy, Devon.

links.title: Plymouth City Council: Tamar-Tavy Estuary SSSI
links.description: Introduction to the designated Site of Special Scientific Interest north west of Plymouth, from the Tamar Bridge upstream to includes the Tamerton Creek.

1065112.title: Thames
1065112.description:
The River Thames is most noted as flowing tbrough the capital of the United Kingdom, London.
By this point, the river is tidal, and known as the Tidestream of the Thames, which stretches east beyond the
Thames Barrier and Dartford Crossing, becoming Sea Reach east of  Tilbury and  Gravesend.
This region, and the area of sea east to the Dutch coast, separating the North Sea from the  English Channel,
is represented by the  Thames Estuary category.
Before London there are many tributaries flowing into the Thames, but perhaps the most significant is below  Dorchester, Oxfordshire, where the River Thame joins the River Isis.
West of this confluence, despite the name, the Isis is considered as the Thames, with its source at springs north of  Kemble, Gloucestershire.

links.title: Wikipedia: Crossings of the River Thames
links.description: Article on history and currently 200 bridges, 27 tunnels, six public ferries, one cable car link, and one ford near the source all the way to the estuary barrier. Comprises tables providing traffic type, GPS coordinates, date opened and links for further details within the online encyclopedia.

links.title: Thames Explorer Trust
links.description: Charity promoting education, physical access, to the tidal region from Isleworth to Greenwich.

links.title: Where Thames Smooth Waters Glide
links.description: Historical resource with illustrated maps, literary references, details, including aerial views, old and modern photos, of the estuary around QEII bridge through London to Thames Head.

links.title: Thames Discovery Programme
links.description: Archaeological project to record and collect artifacts exposed at low tide along the banks at low tide, concentrating on the city of London. Includes links to videos, photo galleries, and social media.

links.title: Thames Pathway
links.description: Journal of a walk down the River Thames by Keith Pauling.

links.title: Gov UK: Thames Enforcement Plan
links.description: An annual overview of enforcement activity planned for the non-tidal river, aimed to stop illegal activity, correct environmental harm, whether restoration or remediation, and provide regulatory control and guidance where appropriate.

1053374.title: Wye
1053374.description:
This category is for geographical websites devoted to the River Wye, ranking fifth-longest river in the UK.
The source in North Wales, with the first tributary, Afon Tarennig, at its first bridge, the A44, Pont Rhydgaled.
The first major settlement is ar  Llangurig, where the Wye flows south with the A470 on its east bank.
Then at Rhadader (Rhaeadr Gwy), Llanwrthwl, Newbury-on-Wye, to  Builth Wells (Llanfair-ym-Muallt),
where the A470 crosses and continues south on the west bank.
A bridge leaves the A470, north of Erwood to join the B4594 to Painscastle, or north back to Aberedw,
where the tributary, the River Edw joins the Wye from the east.
A bridge also leaves the A470 between Boughrood and Llyswen, where the Wye the flows northwest,
bridged by the A468 at Glasbury, onwards to  Hay-on-Wye, before leaving Powys for Herfordshire.
The River Wye continues east flowing through  Hereford, meandering south to  Ross-on-Wye, where its
is crossed by the A40, which follows the west bank, as the Wye meanders south west, north west of the 
Forest of Dean, to  Goodrich, and  Monmouth flowing south, forming the border with England, to its mouth
at  Chepstow, into the mouth of the Severn, where it is spanned by the Severn Suspension Bridge at  Sedbury.

links.title: Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty
links.description: Describes the landscape, wildlife and heritage of the area, straddling the Welsh and English border counties; includes information about conservation, and for visitors.

links.title: Wikipedia: River Wye
links.description: Article updated by the public about the river from its source on Plynlimon, meandering between Wales and England borders,to the Severn estuary. Includes history, cultural references, and conversation, images of bridges, and links to related articles.

links.title: The Wye and Usk Foundation
links.description: Charity concerned with the conservation, rehabilitation and improvement of indigenous species of fish, animal and plant life, promoting responsible fishing. History, ecology, restoration projects, volunteers, administration, and contacts.

531202.title: Wildlife
531202.description: Websites about animals (including mammals, birds, reptiles, fish, insects, mollusks, etc.) and plants (including vascular plants, nonvascular plants, fungi, lichens, etc.) living and growing wild in the United Kingdom, whether native or introduced.

links.title: Naturenet: UK Countryside & Nature Conservation
links.description: Aims to provide a resource for practical nature conservation and management. Includes articles about law, education, careers and training, agencies and organisations, and links to environmental discussion groups.

links.title: Natural History Pictures
links.description: A picture library of 20,000 images, covering natural history and the environment in Great Britain and Western Europe. Includes a list of lectures topics available, a diary, and links to related web sites.

links.title: UK Safari
links.description: Information about wildlife and the countryside. Contains articles, photographs, a newsletter, a list of rescue hospitals, and links to related web sites.

links.title: Wild Boar in Britain
links.description: Information on free living wild boar. Includes field signs, academic and research papers, a forum, locations of breeding populations, and a study of the historical importance of the species.

links.title: Wildlife Online UK
links.description: Aims to provide a useful and educational resource, drawing information from textbooks and scientific papers. Contains details of the natural history of several British species, with images, and links to related sites.

links.title: The Shark Trust
links.description: Promotes the study, management and conservation of sharks, skates and rays in the UK and elsewhere. Includes news, photographs, a video, a forum, links to related sites, and the opportunity to adopt a shark.

links.title: Marine Life Information Network
links.description: Information about the biology and sensitivity of marine habitats, communities and species around Britain and Ireland. Includes data access, educational resources, species recording schemes, newsletters, reports, and frequently asked questions.

links.title: Reptiles and Amphibians of the UK (RAUK)
links.description: Information and discussion about the identification of snakes, lizards, newts, frogs, toads, tadpoles, and spawn. Includes links to related sites and organisations, advice on herpetofauna, and a forum.

links.title: Badgerland
links.description: Description of the births, deaths, family life, and setts of badgers. Includes activities, educational material, and legal information.

links.title: Bat Conservation Trust
links.description: Detailed information about the species and habitats, monitoring, legislation and protection, training courses, news and events.

links.title: Wild Guide UK
links.description: Photographs of grasshoppers, crickets, butterflies and moths, true bugs, and flies, displayed to enable comparison. Includes a description and identification markings for each species.

links.title: The Wildfowl & Wetlands Trust
links.description: Engendering care and concern for wetlands by focusing on rare wetland birds and bringing people into close contact with ducks, geese, and swans at centres throughout the UK. Includes research information, news and events, and learning resource materials.

links.title: Wild Flower Page
links.description: Describes the first steps in finding and studying wild flowers. Includes a flower-of-the-month feature and information about conservation, wildlife news items, and links to related sites.

links.title: British Trees
links.description: Describes native trees and woodlands. Includes a species guide, images and photomicrographs, bibliography, magazine list, and links to related sites and organisations.

links.title: Wildlife Gardening
links.description: Describes how to make any garden a haven for wildlife. Includes news and features, project tutorials and a message board.

links.title: British Mycological Society
links.description: Aims to promote the study of fungi. Provides news items, details of meetings, educational resources and publications.

links.title: First Nature
links.description: Illustrated guide to the birds, land mammals, fishes, insects, reptiles, amphibians, fungi, trees, and wild flowers of Britain and Europe. Includes contact information and links to related sites.

links.title: Plantlife
links.description: A charity which carries out plant species and habitat conservation, owns and manages nature reserves, campaigns, and raises awareness through education. Includes detailed species information, surveys and sections on nature reserves, important plant areas, and opportunities to volunteer.

links.title: Barn Owl Centre of Gloucestershire
links.description: Dedicated to the welfare and conservation needs of owls and other birds of prey, whether their origin is wild or captive bred.

links.title: The Hawk Conservancy Trust
links.description: A country park in Andover, Hampshire, where birds of prey perform flying demonstrations. Includes information on species, activities, conservation, education, research, membership, sponsorship, and opening times and prices.

links.title: The Scottish Sealife Sanctuary
links.description: A centre on the shores of Loch Creran, near Oban, providing an aquarium and a rescue and rehabilitation facility for common and grey seal pups. Includes contact details, and information about seals and otters.

links.title: Cwm Elan Estate and Trust
links.description: Elan Valley is an internationally important wildlife site of over 70 square miles, leased to a trust. Includes details of flora and fauna and full events calendar.

links.title: ORCA
links.description: Dedicated to the protection of cetaceans, through research, partnership and education. Includes news, a guide to species identification, photographs, a sightings list, and links to related sites.

links.title: British Pteridological Society
links.description: Describes their activities and provides images and information about species and habitats. Includes details of projects and links to related sites.

links.title: Wild-Live
links.description: Nature awareness and outdoor tracking school in Co. Armagh. Includes photographs and information about weekend and one-day programs.

links.title: WildCRU Wildlife Conservation Research Unit
links.description: Oxford University group develops practical solutions to conservation problems through research, implementation, education and local public involvement. Includes support and donation details.

links.title: Sea Shore Antics
links.description: Provides a glimpse into what some of the UK sea shore inhabitants actually get up to, when undisturbed by humans.

links.title: British Marine Life Study Society
links.description: A natural history organisation dedicated to the study of the marine fauna and flora of the shore and seas surrounding the British Isles. Includes articles, newsletter, news bulletin service, and links to related sites.

links.title: British Wildlife Centre
links.description: A natural setting where the public can see animals, birds, and reptiles. Includes opening times and prices, list of facilities, interactive map, conservation information and educational resources, and links to related sites.

links.title: Nature in Shetland
links.description: News of the latest sightings and information about marine life, birds, insects and amphibians. Includes articles, photographs, details of educational courses, events and publications, and links to related sites and organisations.

links.title: English Country Garden
links.description: A catalogue of birds, animals, flowers and trees found in an English Country Garden.

links.title: UK Moths

531906.title: Aberdeen, City of
531906.description: Aberdeen is a unitary authority and is also the HQ for Aberdeenshire. ('The Granite City')   Some of the local areas include: Bridge of Don Bucksburn  Cove Bay Cults Denmore Dyce  Kingswells Peterculter   Occupies, for the most part, undulating land between the mouths of the River Don to the north and the River Dee to the south. Granted a royal charter in 1179.   Aberdeen grew up as two separate burghs - Old Aberdeen at the mouth of the Don and New Aberdeen, a fishing and trading settlement where the Denburn entered the Dee estuary.   In 1495 William Elphinstone, Bishop of Aberdeen (1483-1514), founded King's College.   A century later in 1593 the Protestant George Keith, founded the University of Marischal College which boasts the world's second largest granite building. The two universities were eventually united in 1860.   Robert Gordon's College, which was founded in 1730, was constituted as a university in 1992.   Dominated by oil and gas-related industries, engineering, fish processing, papermaking, textiles, information technology and construction and transport industries.

One of the Slate Islands, Seil is a small island on the east side of the Firth of Lorn, 7 miles south-west of Oban. It has been linked to the Scottish mainland since 1792 when the Clachan Bridge, also known as the Bridge Over the Atlantic, was built by engineer Robert Mylne.

Main settlements are Balvicar and Ellenabeich, which is also known as Easdale.

533400.title: Clackmannanshire
533400.description: Clackmannanshire occupies territory between the Ochil Hills to the north, which rise to heights of more than 2,000 feet, and the River Forth to the south. It comprises a lowland plain forming the valleys of the River Forth and of the River Devon which joins the Forth near Cambus.   Affectionately remembered as the 'Wee County', Clackmannanshire was Britain's smallest county prior to its inclusion in Central Region between 1975 and 1996. A local government area once again, Clackmannanshire is the second smallest, after Dundee City, of Scotland's new unitary authorities.

This category leads specifically to websites offering holiday accommodation in Dumfries and Galloway.
Those only providing facilities for visitors to set up their tent, camper, RV, motor home or caravan are given the parallel topic of  Camping and Caravans
That is where Glamping sites are currently listed.
Where those websites also offer static caravans, and on-site entertainment they may be assigned the topic  Accommodation: Resorts .
The Accommodation category is most commonly divided into  Bed and Breakfast ,  Hotels and  Self Catering .
Some of these websites may have camp site facilities in addition, and only if the primary facilities
offered, span more that one of these will the website not be assigned to a sub-topic.

533209.title: Moray
533209.description: Moray is a unitary authority stretching along the north east coast of Scotland.  Comprising a natural and man made landscape of remarkable diversity from the high peaks of the Cairngorms through rolling hills to the Laich of Moray, a fertile tract of lowland.     Being protected by the sweep of the Cairngorm Mountains and having the benefit of the Atlantic Drift to warm its coastal waters gives Moray a milder climate than the rest of the country.   The capital town, Elgin, thrives as a centre of administration, education, tourism and trade with agricultural, service and textile industries.  It was one of the first Scots burghs created in the 12th century by David I. Occupying a strategic site on the route from Aberdeen to Inverness, its ruined castle was the reputed scene of the murder of King Duncan by Macbeth.    Moray is distillery country, "Rome was built on seven hills, and Dufftown built on seven stills," and many well known malt whiskies are distilled within the boundaries of Moray.   Moray is home to two Royal Air Force bases, RAF Kinloss and RAF Lossiemouth. RAF Kinloss is situated beside Findhorn Bay on the coast, a little north of Forres. The large base is home to the RAF's entire Nimrod MR2 fleet. RAF Lossiemouth, situated 5 miles north of Elgin, is one of the RAF's most important bases hosting 4 front-line primary attack squadrons of Tornado GR1 and GR4's.
